DoorDash is adding Macy's, Anthropologie, and outdoor apparel brands for on-demand clothing delivery
The delivery app is also launching a $7.99 return pickup service, with a nationwide rollout planned for November
By Cris Tolomia·2 min read·Updated October 1, 2026
DoorDash announced partnerships Wednesday with Macy's $M, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans, and Timberland, making products from those retailers available for on-demand delivery through its app.
Macy's will offer apparel, beauty, and home goods from more than 350 stores nationwide, with delivery in as little as two hours, the company said. Anthropologie will make clothing, shoes, accessories, beauty, and home décor available from more than 220 stores. The North Face, Vans, and Timberland — all brands owned by VF Corporation $VFC — will ship from a combined network of more than 350 stores.
The Macy's partnership also extends to marketing: DoorDash will debut a float called "Dashing All the Way by DoorDash" in the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade this fall. The companies have had a prior commercial relationship since 2020, when DoorDash began handling Macy's first-party delivery through its Drive On-Demand service.
DoorDash is simultaneously introducing a return service. Customers who want to send back an eligible retail purchase can pay a flat fee of $7.99 for a courier to pick up the item from their door in as little as 30 minutes and return it to the store. No box or prepaid label is required, the company said. The service is available in select cities and is expected to expand across the country in November.
The new retail names extend a push that has seen DoorDash add Costco $COST, Gap $GPS, Kohl's $KSS, Barnes & Noble, and SKIMS earlier this year. The company said more than half of the NRF Top 100 Retailers now partner with the platform. The Wall Street Journal reported that DoorDash's directly sold product catalog reached roughly 30 million items as of June, compared with about nine million a year earlier.
Macy's Chief Customer and Digital Officer Max Magni told the Journal the retailer hopes to attract new customers through the partnership. Macy's will also make fast delivery a more prominent option on its own website, he said.
DoorDash Vice President of New Verticals Fuad Hannon told the Journal that five-to-seven-day shipping is no longer acceptable to consumers, a shift he attributed to expectations set by Amazon $AMZN and Walmart $WMT.
Rival Uber $UBER Eats has been pursuing a parallel strategy in the broader competition among delivery apps to become the fulfillment backbone for retail. Uber announced a partnership with Foot Locker $FL in July and expanded Costco delivery nationwide in September, according to WTOP. Costco separately struck a deal with DoorDash this year as well, making it one of several retailers now working with multiple delivery platforms simultaneously.

The drone delivery program aims to combat the hardest part of autonomous delivery: the first and last ten feet. Picking up an order from a kitchen and laying it safely on the customer’s doorstep are the most challenging steps in the food delivery process, according to DoorDash.

The aircrafts have six slow-spinning propellers and their noise projection is “limited to roughly that of a passing car at delivery height,” the company claims.

DoorDash Air combines a new six-propeller aircraft with restaurant loading infrastructure and the company’s existing delivery marketplace
DoorDash has unveiled a purpose-built delivery drone and supporting system for restaurant deliveries. The company will begin piloting DoorDash Air in Northern California.
The announcement provides new details about the aircraft and the infrastructure behind DoorDash’s in-house drone delivery program. DoorDash says the aircraft can handle about 80% of typical restaurant orders on its platform. Initial testing showed average delivery times of under five minutes from the restaurant to the customer’s door.
The program expands DoorDash’s existing drone strategy. The company has already completed tens of thousands of drone deliveries through partnerships with operators including Wing and Flytrex. DoorDash launched its own DoorDash Air program in July after DoorDash Labs received FAA Part 135 air carrier certification.
A Drone Designed Around Restaurant Orders
The new DoorDash aircraft uses six slow-spinning propellers positioned away from the aircraft’s arms to reduce noise. At cruising altitude, DoorDash says its sound is comparable to a passing car.
The aircraft was designed around the size and weight of restaurant orders. DoorDash estimates that about 80% of typical orders are light and small enough for the aircraft to carry safely. The company notes that the estimate comes from a limited sample of U.S. restaurant deliveries.
DoorDash also says initial tests produced average delivery times of less than five minutes between the restaurant and customer. The company cautions that the estimate comes from deliveries of limited distance and size. Delivery times are not guaranteed.
The Northern California pilot will include Chipotle Mexican Grill, Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen and Momo N Curry among its first restaurant partners.
Building the System Around the Restaurant
DoorDash is positioning the aircraft as one part of a larger delivery system. The company has also developed the merchant handoff process, ground infrastructure and software needed to route orders.
The approach addresses a practical challenge for restaurant drone delivery. Restaurants already have established kitchen workflows and limited space. Requiring specialized infrastructure could make drone delivery harder to adopt.
DoorDash says it has developed several loading options that fit into existing restaurant operations. The goal is to let businesses use drone delivery without major changes to their facilities or workflows.
Harrison Shih, Head of DoorDash Air, said the company designed the system around that requirement.
“We didn’t start with a drone and ask what would fit. We started with what people order and how local businesses actually operate, then built the entire system from there.”
The approach also marks a shift from DoorDash’s earlier drone deployments. The company has worked with third-party drone operators while integrating drone delivery into its ordering platform. DoorDash launched service with Flytrex in the Dallas-Fort Worth area in 2025 and has also expanded its partnership with Wing across several U.S. markets.
With DoorDash Air, the company is adding its own aircraft and delivery system while continuing to work with outside drone partners.
DoorDash is integrating DoorDash Air into its Autonomous Delivery Platform, which determines how individual orders should be delivered.
Depending on the order, the platform can select a human Dasher, DoorDash’s Dot delivery robot, a drone or a delivery partner. This allows DoorDash to use drones for orders that fit the aircraft while routing other deliveries through different methods.
DoorDash says its marketplace currently routes about 10 million orders each day. That volume gives the platform a large pool of deliveries from which to identify orders suited to autonomous systems.
The company has also identified longer local trips as an area where drones could play a role. DoorDash reported in July that more than 20% of its 2025 orders traveled three to five miles. Those orders took nearly 25% longer on average than shorter deliveries, partly because matching them with a Dasher took longer.
DoorDash Air therefore represents more than a new delivery aircraft. The company is building drones into the same platform that decides how millions of local orders move from merchants to customers. The Northern California pilot will provide an early test of how that end-to-end model works in restaurant operations.

DoorDash is launching new ways to use the local delivery platform, including text message ordering, drone deliveries, and retail returns. The idea is to prevent you from missing the return window for unwanted products purchased on DoorDash due to other commitments that prevent you from shipping or taking it back yourself. TikTok announced its own version of this feature via UPS yesterday.

Home All News USA New York City Collects $131 Million From DoorDash for Delivery Workers Unfairly...
The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) announced a historic $131.5 million enforcement action against DoorDash for systematic violations of the local Delivery Worker Laws.
The settlement will place more than $115 million directly into the pockets of delivery workers and pay for $16 million in civil penalties and costs. More than 260,000 workers were underpaid by DoorDash, including workers who were not paid at all, or were paid late for work they had already performed.
It’s the largest worker settlement in New York City history.
“DoorDash underpaid more than 260,000 workers, and today we are getting that money back,” said Mayor Mamdani. “When a worker earns a wage, they deserve to be paid that wage, on time and in full.”
He reminded the public that no corporation is above the law—especially when it earns $13.7 billion in revenue, like DoorDash did in 2025, a 28% increase compared to their 2024 revenue of $10.72 billion.
“Today, New York City’s delivery workers are showing that opaque algorithms will not have the final word when it comes to how much they are paid for the hard work they do,” said DCWP Commissioner Samuel A.A. Levine.
The settlement is about more than recovering money that workers are owed. It also puts in place a new monitoring system ensuring DoorDash follows the law going forward—one that gives workers a direct role in identifying violations and gives the City data it needs to act.
A Princeton University partner, the Workers’ Algorithm Observatory, will develop software that will allow the drivers to share their DoorDash trip and earnings data directly with the agency. It will allow DCWP to monitor DoorDash’s compliance with minimum pay, maximum trip distances, trip disclosures, pay transparency, and tip transparency.
DCWP’s citywide investigation began after dozens of workers filed reports with the Department.
The agency found that DoorDash failed to pay thousands of workers at all for work they had performed and failed to pay thousands more on time. These workers will receive compensation calculated at approximately 200% of the amount they were underpaid.
For example, a worker who was owed $1,000 but received no payment will receive $3,000. A worker who was paid $1,000 later than allowed under the law will receive $2,000.
Workers don’t even need to file a claim or submit evidence to receive payment. DCWP has identified all individuals owed money through its analysis of DoorDash’s records—and payments will be sent out this fall.
MORE IMPROVEMENTS FOR NYC: New York City is Putting ‘The Park’ Back in Park Avenue – And Adding a Protected Bike Lane (LOOK)
The case’s Settlement Administrator will send personalized emails to each worker who experienced an underpayment from April 22, 2022 to June 28, 2026. Workers will be able to choose between an electronic payment and a check by mail.
More details of the case is available at nyc.gov/doordash.
As part of the investigation, DCWP obtained terabytes of data from DoorDash, including billions of rows documenting the company’s treatment of delivery workers. DCWP’s Research and Analytics Division analyzed the data to identify more than 152 million individual payment transactions and 110 million working hours connected to the investigation.
DoorDash will be required to make software updates to prevent the company from offering a delivery to a worker in New York City unless that worker’s time is being recorded as compensable on-call time or trip time. The updates will also provide workers with additional information about their work time and pay and ensure DoorDash complies with the Minimum Pay Rule for “batched” trips, ending the unlawful practice of paying a lower rate for certain legs of a trip.
“Amidst a cost of living crisis, delivery workers deserve to rest assured that work completed means compensation earned,” said Council Member and Consumer and Worker Protection Chair Harvey Epstein.
The city passed a minimum wage law in 2021 which is adjusted annually for inflation and currently sits at $22.13 per hour.
“DoorDash thought they could shortchange their workers and get away with it,” said Council Member Sandy Nurse. “As DoorDash pulls in record profits, the workers who make them rich are entitled to their fair share.”

DoorDash is expanding further into the fashion and apparel world, unveiling shoppers can now buy goods from Macy’s, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland directly from its retail marketplace.
The same-day delivery platform is also throwing its hat into the retail returns ecosystem with the launch of the Dasher Returns. Customers seeking to return an eligible retail purchase pay a flat fee of $7.99 for a courier to pick up the item from their door in as little as 30 minutes and return it to the store.

No box or prepaid label is required, DoorDash said. The service is available in select cities and is expected to expand across the U.S. in November.
The company revealed the product updates at its annual Dash Forward event Tuesday.
“This is what we mean by the mall in your pocket: the brands you already know and trust, on the shelf near you, delivered as easily as walking into the mall used to be. You can get Macy’s or Anthropologie in as little as an hour, and return it just as easily if it’s not right, no box, no label, back on the shelf and the money back in your pocket,” said Shanna Prevé, chief revenue officer at DoorDash in a statement. “For retailers, it means turning the stores they already have into a growth channel, not a warehouse three states away.”
At the event, Prevé told attendees DoorDash expects to make 80 percent of the retail orders it handles eligible for Dasher Returns by the end of 2026.
“Because that inventory goes back on the shelves today, Gap (a DoorDash partner) has a chance to resell it to another mom, and I get my refund in days, not weeks,” said Prevé.
Macy’s has partnered with DoorDash since 2020, with the department store enabling shoppers to select same-day delivery on its website via the platform’s Drive On-Demand service.
With the expanded collaboration, consumers can now find Macy’s assortment on the DoorDash Marketplace both online and in DoorDash’s mobile app, with the retailer offering two-hour delivery from more than 350 of its roughly 430 locations.
According to a report from The Wall Street Journal, Macy’s will make DoorDash’s delivery option more prominent on its own website. Previously, DoorDash branding was not included.
Anthropologie’s available assortment can be delivered from its more than 220 stores nationwide, while the three VF Corporation-owned brands can ship products from over 350 U.S. locations.
DoorDash, which is known largely for conducting restaurant and grocery delivery via a network of independent drivers, has scaled its retail footprint over the past year as it aims to tackle more of the last mile of the supply chain.
In 2026, retailers including Kohl’s, Carter’s, Costco, Gap, Anthropologie’s sister brand Urban Outfitters, Steve Madden, Dolce Vita and Hibbett have all joined DoorDash’s apparel marketplace. The companies joined a growing list including Old Navy, Pacsun, Dick’s Sporting Goods, Academy Sports + Outdoors, David’s Bridal and JD Sports, all of whom now can ship parcels same day from their stores.
Outside the Dasher Returns launch, returns for goods initially delivered via DoorDash are settled through each merchant’s own policy. To get a refund, shoppers have to initiate the return in the DoorDash app, take the item to the store, show an in-app return barcode and upload a photo of the return receipt.
DoorDash says that review process, including the refund, takes place in about four business days.
The terms are not uniform across the marketplace. For example, DoorDash offers Macy’s consumers free in-store only, 30-day returns. However, orders placed Oct. 5 through Dec. 31 can be returned through Jan. 31, 2027.
Anthropologie’s policy allows DoorDash purchases to be exchanged for the same product in a new size or color within 30 days at any of its stores. But the company explicitly states items are not eligible for refund or return.
Aside from the reveal of its new partnerships and returns offerings, DoorDash used the Dash Forward event to give more updates on its DoorDash Air drone delivery offering.
Pilot drone deliveries will begin in Northern California in partnership with national restaurant brands including Chipotle and Popeyes, the company said.
The delivery company has not revealed if any apparel or retail clients will be included in the pilots, and there has been no announcement when the drone deliveries will be available to consumers.
DoorDash says estimates from the initial tests indicate that deliveries arrive at the consumer’s door in under five minutes on average.
A week ahead of the event, DoorDash also introduced Brand Center, a platform giving merchant shelf-level visibility into their DoorDash performance. It surfaces on-shelf availability and out-of-stock trends across stores, shows what shoppers substitute when an item is unavailable and lets eligible brands edit product images, descriptions and categories directly.

DoorDash Debuts Returns Program Amid New Retail Partnerships
DoorDash launched a returns program along with an expansion of its retail marketplace, according to a Wednesday (Sept. 30) press release.
The expansion involves partnerships in the apparel, beauty and home spaces, with Macy’s, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland now available options to customers, the release said.
“This is what we mean by the mall in your pocket: the brands you already know and trust, on the shelf near you, delivered as easily as walking into the mall used to be,” DoorDash Chief Revenue Officer Shanna Prevé said in the release. “You can get Macy’s or Anthropologie in as little as an hour and return it just as easily if it’s not right, no box, no label, back on the shelf and the money back in your pocket. For retailers, it means turning the stores they already have into a growth channel, not a warehouse three states away.”

The returns are possible via Dasher Returns, which lets consumers pay a flat $7.99 fee to schedule a return for an eligible retail order, and a Dasher can retrieve it from their door in as quickly as 30 minutes and bring it back to the store, according to the release. Pricing and times are subject to change.
“The return is processed on the spot, the item can go directly back on the shelf, and the consumer receives their refund within days,” the release said.
DoorDash also announced several other products and services Wednesday as it held its Dash Forward 2026 event.
These include the ability to place orders with DoorDash by sending a text rather than using an app or browser; the ability to connect DoorDash to compatible internal AI tools so employees can order team lunches or items for office restocking; a platform called DoorDash OS that connects all the DoorDash tools that are used by restaurants; a new AI assistant called DashBuddy that answers questions for Dashers; and a planned upcoming drone delivery system that will serve local businesses, the company said in several press releases issued Wednesday.
DoorDash last week announced a drone delivery partnership with Lowe’s and Google’s Wing, PYMNTS reported Thursday (Sept. 24).
The move and others like it are giving retailers a way to find out what delivery speed is worth, PYMNTS reported Friday (Sept. 25). More than 20% of orders on the DoorDash platform last year traveled between three and five miles, but those orders took almost 25% longer than shorter deliveries, mainly because pairing them with a driver took longer. Drone-delivered orders arrived in an average of 25 minutes during 2025, while some locations taking part in partner drone pilots saw order volumes grow by around 30%.
“Whether the arithmetic works will depend heavily on cost,” the report said, citing Barclays research showing autonomous delivery costs below that of conventional delivery. “Cutting several dollars from fulfillment does more to improve the economics of delivering a $15 order than a $150 order.”

DoorDash launches retail returns service, self-designed drones
DoorDash Air is a new drone delivery service that the company will operate using its own self-built aircraft rather than an outside supplier. (Photo: DoorDash)
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 10:03 AM PDT 5 min read
DoorDash is entering the reverse logistics market and leaning heavily into drone delivery, announcing on Wednesday that it has launched a new retail returns service and a custom-built drone delivery system for time-sensitive orders in another modal expansion of its last-mile logistics network.
They were among a series of product releases and enhancements, unveiled at a big user event, aimed at making shopping and ordering food, grocery and retail items more convenient.
The returns program is live in select cities and is expected to roll out nationwide in November using the same gig driver pool that delivers from stores to homes, the tech platform said. Consumers pay a flat $7.99 for Dasher Returns — no box or label required. DoorDash (NASDAQ: DASH) said drivers will pick up return orders in as fast as 30 minutes and return them to the store, which will process the return and issue a refund within days.
By offering returns, DoorDash is moving into a space that offers higher margins than store-to-door delivery and taking on parcel shipping incumbents like FedEx and UPS that are focusing more on returns than short-distance delivery in the B2C e-commerce market. FedEx last year began offering a lower cost version of its no-box, no-label returns to make it easier for customers to return unwanted merchandise, but the service requires consumers to drop off the goods at outlets such as FedEx Office and Kohl's store locations.
Earlier this year, Uber Eats introduced a service that allows customers to return goods ordered through its app for a fee.
But it's an open question whether consumers are willing to pay for returns when there is less urgency than with an inbound order and they can wait to drop it off at a store themselves for free.
"For retailers, it means turning the stores they already have into a growth channel, not a warehouse three states away," said Chief Revenue Officer Shanna Prevé in a news release.
Meanwhile, DoorDash has added to the growing number of retailers who have linked their product catalogs to its marketplace. Shoppers can now use the DoorDash app to order goods from Macy's, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland and receive fast delivery. Costco and Skims began delivery partnerships with DoorDash earlier this month.
DoorDash calls its retail product "Mall-in-Your-Pocket" because consumers can shop for apparel, beauty and home goods with fast delivery from hundreds of stores nationwide on one platform.
DoorDash also recently introduced new ways for retailers and brands to grow. Brand Center gives participating brands real-time visibility into inventory on store shelves and shopper substitution trends, helping them understand how their products are showing up in stores and what shoppers choose when an item is unavailable.
DoorDash also said it is investing in its own drone delivery operation, offering customers a faster delivery option from local restaurants and convenience stores.
The delivery platform's in-house robotics and automation division, DoorDash Labs, made the six-rotor drones on its own. Until now, DoorDash has relied on outside drone operators like Alphabet's Wing and Flytrex to conduct the actual aerial deliveries. Lowe's, for example, this month began a pilot program for drone delivery in North Carolina enabled by the DoorDash marketplace and Wing's small, unmanned aerial vehicles.
"We'll continue our partnership with third parties like Wing and Flytrex, but in the same way we use multiple delivery methods, having multiple drone delivery options adds resilience to our network and helps us better serve merchants and bring the benefits of drone delivery to more communities faster," said spokesman Eli Scheinholtz in an email exchange.
DoorDash said it closely consulted with businesses to design everything from packaging, to loading systems and ground handoffs. It is building an array of loading options designed to fit into existing business operations and make drone delivery feasible for local businesses of all sizes.
About 80% of typical DoorDash restaurant orders are light and small enough for the aircraft to carry safely.
"Any local business should be able to reach consumers by air. We built the whole system so that they can deliver by air without being disruptive to how they run their business," said Harrison Shih, head of DoorDash Air, in the announcement.
Trial flights are underway in Northern California with national brands Chipotle and Popeyes, and local restaurants. Delivery times have averaged less than five minutes so far, DoorDash said.
Customers can choose on the app whether their order is delivered by a driver, its self-designed small robot or a drone. An autonomous system uses smart routing, incorporating factors like weather, flight range, and ground traffic to narrow down which orders actually make sense to send by air. Using the app, customers can select whether a driver, a Dot robot or a drone is the best delivery option.
The drone's cruising noise is similar to that of a passing car. Orders are picked up and lowered to the ground with a winch, with a backup option to safely lower the aircraft to the ground in rare events, DoorDash said. Amazon drones, by contrast, drop boxes at their destination from about 13 feet in the air.
In other news, DoorDash also introduced text ordering, allowing customers to simply send a text describing what they want from a restaurant or grocery store without the need to fiddle with an app or browser.
Why It Matters: DoorDash is a giant platform that is leveraging its technology to push more and more into retail parcel delivery and becoming a competitor to other courier companies.

DoorDash’s $300 Million Grubhub Deal Opens a New Venue-Commerce Opportunity
DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH) is acquiring Wonder's Grubhub Campus Dining business for $300 million and investing another $125 million in Wonder's Series D. The campus business operates at more than 450 colleges and universities, allowing students to order from campus dining facilities, pay with dining dollars, and schedule pickup. DoorDash plans to expand the technology beyond campuses into stadiums, hotels and similar venues, with the transaction expected to close in the first half of 2027.
The deal fits DoorDash's broader push beyond conventional restaurant delivery. Its Q2 2026 Marketplace GOV rose 36% to $33.1 billion, while orders increased 27% to 970 million. Even excluding Deliveroo, GOV growth was still 23%, showing that DoorDash has meaningful underlying momentum to support new verticals.
DoorDash’s $300 Million Grubhub Deal Opens a New Venue-Commerce Opportunity
Strong Cash Generation Supports DoorDash's Latest Expansion Bet
The strongest upside is the potential to turn an established campus ordering network into a broader venue-commerce platform. With more than 450 universities already using the technology, DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH) is acquiring an existing merchant and consumer infrastructure rather than building a campus product from scratch. Extending that vertically integrated ordering and pickup system into stadiums, hotels, and other controlled environments could increase order density and create additional Commerce Platform revenue without relying entirely on traditional restaurant delivery.
The $300 million purchase is also relatively modest against DoorDash's financial scale. The company generated $742 million of free cash flow in Q2 alone, up from $355 million a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA reached $914 million, up 40%. That gives DoorDash capacity to fund the acquisition without putting significant pressure on near-term liquidity.
The Wonder investment adds another strategic option. Wonder has expanded to 157 locations, more than quadrupling its footprint since early 2025, while investing in robotics and AI. DoorDash therefore gains exposure to technology that could eventually improve food preparation, fulfillment, and delivery economics, potentially supporting longer-term margin expansion if automation becomes commercially viable.
The Deal's Near-Term Earnings Impact Could Remain Limited
The immediate financial contribution from Grubhub Campus Dining is unlikely to be material relative to DoorDash's existing scale. DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH) generated $4.45 billion of revenue and $33.1 billion of Marketplace GOV in Q2, meaning the $300 million acquisition is strategically significant but unlikely by itself to materially change consolidated earnings. The larger valuation argument depends on successfully expanding the campus technology into new venues, something that remains unproven.
There is also execution risk from expanding into businesses with different operating requirements. DoorDash is already investing heavily in its global technology platform and international operations, while Q2 research and development expense rose to $535 million from $351 million a year earlier. Adding a new venue-focused platform could increase spending before the economics of stadiums, hotels and other locations are established.
The $125 million Wonder investment carries an additional risk because Wonder remains in an aggressive expansion phase. Its footprint has quadrupled since the start of 2025, and it plans to enter Texas in 2027. DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH) is therefore committing capital to a business pursuing physical expansion and robotics investment whose returns may take years to materialize.
The partnership is strategically positive for DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH) because it expands the company into controlled, high-density venues while adding technology that could be reused beyond college campuses. DoorDash's 23% organic GOV growth, rising adjusted EBITDA, and $742 million quarterly free cash flow provide a strong financial foundation for the move.
However, the $300 million acquisition is unlikely to materially affect near-term earnings, making the investment case dependent on DoorDash successfully scaling the platform into stadiums, hotels, and other venues. The deal therefore strengthens DoorDash's long-term growth optionality more than its immediate financial outlook.
While we acknowledge the potential of DASH as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. A revised takeover agreement is lifting both the buyer and the target in a chip deal that just got simpler. On Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) stock is at $86.64, up 8% in morning trading. This follows the company replacing its $7 billion all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) with a $5.7 billion all-cash bid.
Synaptics stock is up 14% to $121.32, a larger climb tied to a fixed cash price replacing a floating share exchange.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $590.75, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $752.16, up 1.36%. That gap shows how much of the move traces to the deal itself.

CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated: “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration.” Funding comes from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing.
Dilution Fades for On Semiconductor, Certainty Arrives for Synaptics
For On Semiconductor shareholders, the core change is the removal of dilution. Paying cash leaves the share count untouched, protecting buyback work that included $332 million of repurchases in Q2 2026.
A fixed cash price gives Synaptics investors certainty, and the Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.

On Semiconductor management stated on the August 3 earnings call that Synaptics’ “market-leading connected compute capabilities” complement On Semiconductor’s “strength in power, sensing, and control.”

The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the deal, but other jurisdictions are still reviewing it, and Synaptics shareholders must vote. On August 3, On Semiconductor expected the transaction to close in mid-2027.

Immediate accretion and an AI data center business where management expects revenue to more than double in 2026 support the optimistic view (we covered seven suppliers riding that same AI infrastructure expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). Risks center on new leverage and integrating Synaptics.

ON Semiconductor (ON) Switches to $5.7B All-Cash Synaptics Acquisition, Stock Jumps 6%
By Trader EdgeOctober 2, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
ON Semiconductor restructured its Synaptics acquisition into an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $5.7 billion, reduced from the initial $7 billion stock-based proposal.
Synaptics shareholders will receive $123 cash per share rather than the previously agreed 1.350 ON shares from the June announcement.
ON stock surged approximately 6% during premarket hours, while Synaptics shares climbed roughly 14%.
The restructured agreement eliminates shareholder dilution concerns for ON investors and promises immediate accretion to non-GAAP earnings.
Completion of the transaction requires Synaptics shareholder approval and regulatory clearances, with an expected closing date in mid-2027.
Shares of ON Semiconductor rallied approximately 6% in Friday’s premarket session following the company’s announcement of a restructured takeover agreement with Synaptics. The stock had ended Thursday’s session at $80.08.
Synaptics shares posted even stronger gains, climbing approximately 14% on the announcement. Both semiconductor companies specialize in chip technologies for automotive, industrial, and Internet of Things applications.
The initial agreement, announced in June, proposed an all-stock merger structure. Under those terms, Synaptics shareholders would have exchanged each share for 1.350 ON Semiconductor shares, establishing a transaction value near $7 billion.
The revised agreement converts the transaction to an all-cash purchase. Synaptics shareholders will now receive $123 in cash per share, reducing the total transaction value to approximately $5.7 billion.
The price reduction followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from an unnamed third party. Rather than triggering a competitive bidding situation that elevated the acquisition price, the development prompted both parties to negotiate modified terms more favorable to each company.
ON shareholders sidestep the equity dilution that would have resulted from issuing new shares under the original agreement. This change eliminates a significant concern that had pressured the stock since the June announcement.
The company indicates the restructured transaction will immediately enhance its non-GAAP earnings per share. This represents a meaningful improvement from the original structure, which wasn’t projected to be immediately accretive to earnings.
ON had previously identified $200 million in annual cost synergies from the combination. The company now anticipates additional opportunities, including potential revenue synergies and internalizing certain Synaptics manufacturing operations.
The transaction will be funded through a combination of existing cash reserves and debt financing arranged by Morgan Stanley. The absence of a financing contingency for closing eliminates another potential risk factor.
Synaptics CEO Rahul Patel characterized the cash structure as delivering certainty to investors. “We are providing value certainty at a premium as compared to current value,” he said.
The revised terms present a clear tradeoff. Synaptics shareholders forfeit potential participation in the merged entity’s future performance, receiving instead a guaranteed cash payment.
Robert W. Baird analyst Tristan Gerra maintained a Hold rating on ON stock following the announcement, keeping his $108 price target. The broader Wall Street consensus rates ON a Moderate Buy, while Synaptics carries a Hold rating.
Market timing also worked in the company’s favor. Micron’s impressive earnings results released the previous evening had already elevated semiconductor stocks broadly, providing additional momentum for ON’s announcement heading into Friday’s opening.
Treasury yields retreated from recent peaks that same morning, relieving some pressure on growth-oriented technology stocks.
The acquisition still requires approval from Synaptics shareholders alongside regulatory clearances. While the FTC has already granted approval, reviews in additional jurisdictions remain pending.
The companies are targeting a mid-2027 closing timeline. Between now and then, both stocks will likely respond to progress updates on the approval process.

ON Semiconductor's revised Synaptics deal improves earnings outlook, says BofA
ON Semiconductor’s revised $5.7 billion acquisition of Synaptics could deliver a bigger earnings boost than originally expected while eliminating the share dilution that had weighed on the deal, Bank of America said.
Following an unsolicited competing proposal, the companies amended their June 25 agreement to replace the all-stock transaction with a $123-per-share cash offer.
The deal's aggregate value falls to approximately $5.7 billion from $7 billion, eliminating roughly 59 million additional shares and the previously contemplated 12% to 13% dilution.
With ON Semiconductor shares down 32% since the deal's announcement, Bank of America wrote that revised terms could improve investor reception by removing dilution while preserving the strategic rationale.
ON Semiconductor would fund the deal with cash on hand and approximately $2.5 billion in term loan debt, with no financing condition.
Even with that borrowing, the broker estimates the transaction could increase earnings per share by approximately 11% in calendar 2027 and 15% in calendar 2028.
Its combined-company EPS estimates are $5 and $6.88, respectively, compared with standalone forecasts of $4.51 and $5.99.
Those projected gains reflect an estimated 4% dilution and 2% accretion under the original structure, primarily from eliminating additional shares.
The revised model includes cost synergies of $90 million and $175 million, respectively, partly offset by a roughly $150 million annual financial-income headwind from cash-and-debt funding.
The estimates exclude revenue synergies and potential outsourcing benefits beyond the previously announced $200 million annual cost-synergy target, and management expects to outsource some SYNA production after the first 18 months following closing.
The acquisition would also broaden ON Semiconductor's portfolio, with Bank of America highlighting SYNA's edge computing, connectivity, software, and human-machine interfaces alongside existing power and sensing capabilities.
The broker expects the combination to support more integrated solutions across industrial markets, robotics, autonomous driving, and augmented and virtual reality.
It estimates the acquisition would expand ON Semiconductor's calendar 2030 addressable market by approximately $30 billion to $243 billion.
Bank of America still expects completion by mid-2027, with FTC approval received and other regulatory reviews ongoing.

ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) trades at $68.30 after a brutal summer, while the average Wall Street price target sits at $106.88. That leaves the stock roughly 56% below where analysts, on average, think it should trade.
ON is the Phoenix-based designer behind onsemi, a top supplier of intelligent power and sensing chips for cars, factories, and increasingly, AI server racks. Its EliteSiC silicon carbide and GaNEXUS gallium nitride families are pitched as the plumbing for 800-volt vehicle platforms and the next generation of hyperscaler power trees. Wall Street cares because that story sits at the intersection of two of the biggest capex cycles in tech.
Even after a brutal selloff, business metrics are improving and analysts have not wavered. One has doubled down.
A Three-Month Wipeout in a Rallying Market
Shares of ON have plunged 43.84% over the past three months, a decline steep enough to qualify as a full-blown crash. The stock started that window at $121.62 and has bled all the way down to its current level, with a 14% drop just in the last month.
The selloff came despite strong results. Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue of $1.60 billion beat estimates and rose 9.18% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 topping the $0.7153 consensus. Shares popped more than 5% after the report. The unwind has been driven by broader concerns: high automotive exposure, China cyclicality, a rich trailing valuation, and profit-taking after a run that had ON near $134.92 on a 52-week basis. The peer group softened too, but ON fell harder and faster.
Why Susquehanna Still Sees Roughly 120% Upside
Analysts have not chased the stock lower. Coverage sits at 2 Strong Buy, 11 Buy, 16 Hold, and zero Sell ratings, and estimate revisions have skewed sharply higher, with 25 upward EPS revisions for fiscal 2026 in the trailing 30 days against just two down.
Susquehanna’s Christopher Rolland reiterated a Buy with a Street-high $150 price target, implying roughly 120% upside from $68.30. His thesis: EliteSiC capturing dominant share as EV platforms shift from 400V to 800V architectures, AI data center power scaling through smart power stages and point-of-load converters, and gross margins recovering toward 40%+.
Management backs that narrative. AI data center is now expected to more than double in 2026. CEO Hassane El-Khoury told investors, “Our growth in data center is literally from the wall to the core.” Silicon carbide revenue in data centers is guided to grow nearly 60% year over year, with content per rack jumping from $15,000 to $115,000 in an 800-volt DC architecture. Non-GAAP gross margin already expanded to 39.3%, with Q3 guidance calling for 40% to 42%.
Analog Peers Held Up While ON Broke Down
This selloff is largely a single-name story. Peers softened but held ground.
NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) trades at $227.95 against a target of $311.10, roughly 36% of implied upside. NXPI is up 5.02% year to date with 6 Strong Buy, 16 Buy, 7 Hold and 1 Sell ratings, a solidly bullish tilt.
Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI) has been the sector standout, up 33.72% year to date at $362.65 against a $470.72 target, about 30% upside. Coverage skews aggressively bullish at 7 Strong Buy, 24 Buy, 3 Hold.
ON’s analyst-implied upside is the widest in the group. That makes ON the outlier in the group.
ON trades at $68.30 versus a consensus target of $106.88 from 30 covering analysts, implying 56% upside to the average and about 120% to Susquehanna’s $150. The forward P/E of 16 reflects the sharp fiscal 2026 earnings ramp analysts are modeling toward $3.2028 full-year EPS.
ON is up 26.13% year to date, ahead of the S&P 500‘s 11.85%, but that lead was built and lost in a violent round trip. Over three months, ON’s 43.84% drawdown stands in stark contrast to a flat-to-up broad market.
The bull case for ON here rests on the AI data center ramp and silicon carbide share gains materializing over the next few quarters. Q3 guidance already points to gross margins of 40% to 42%, book-to-bill has been above 1 for several quarters, and lead times have extended to roughly 32 weeks. The bear case centers on automotive weakness in Europe, China exposure, and the pending Synaptics acquisition integration risk are what the market is pricing in. A stalled industrial recovery or a slip in AI content per rack could keep the multiple compressed.
My lean is cautiously bullish. The analyst dispersion is wide for a reason, but the operating data is moving in the bulls’ direction, and ON’s dislocation looks larger than the fundamentals justify.

Synaptics (SYNA) Soars 14% as ON Semi Sweetens Deal With All-Cash Offer
Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) extended its winning streak to a fourth straight session on Friday, surging 14.08 percent on Friday to finish at $121.10 apiece, following ON Semiconductor's decision to switch its acquisition of the former to an all-cash transaction.
Week on week, the stock climbed 17.9 percent.
In an update later Thursday, ON Semiconductor said it is now planning to acquire Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) for $123 per share, down from its original offer of 1.350 ON Semi shares for every SYNA stock held by its shareholders.
Although downsized to $5.7 billion from the original $7 billion, SYNA investors gobbled up its stock to take advantage of the nearly 16 percent premium over its closing price on Thursday.
"By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders," Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) President and CEO Rahul Patel said.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," he noted.
ON Semiconductor is set to finance the transaction through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing from Morgan Stanley.
The transaction is expected to close in the middle of next year, subject to approval of Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) shareholders, while its board of directors will join ON Semiconductor's board.
The acquisition followed Synaptics Inc.'s (NASDAQ:SYNA) soaring losses in both the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2026.
In the last quarter ending June 27, the company said that net losses widened by 9,419 percent to $447.4 million from only $4.7 million in the same period last year, dragged by a $425.3 million non-cash charge related to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US deferred tax assets, which is excluded from non-GAAP results.
Revenues, on the other hand, increased by 8.9 percent to $308 million from $282.8 million year-on-year.
In full fiscal year 2026, net losses soared by 927 percent to $490.8 million from $47.8 million, while revenues increased by 11 percent to $1.197 billion from $1.074 billion last year.
Despite the results, institutional investors remained optimistic about the company's long-term growth prospects, as evidenced by the increase in hedge fund holders establishing exposure, alongside their committed capital.
Insider Monkey data showed that 37 hedge funds held positions in the stock during the period, up from 23 in the first quarter of the year.
More notably, their collective holdings climbed by 77.6 percent to $445.18 million from $250.6 million quarter-on-quarter.

On Semiconductor Climbs 8%, Synaptics Surges 14% as $5.7B Cash Bid Replaces $7B Stock Deal
On Semiconductor scrapped its stock deal for Synaptics and replaced it with cash, and both stocks surged on the news for reasons that point in opposite directions.
Published October 2, 2026, 9:13am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A revised takeover agreement is lifting both the buyer and the target in a chip deal that just got simpler. On Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) stock is at $86.64, up 8% in morning trading. This follows the company replacing its $7 billion all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) with a $5.7 billion all-cash bid.
Synaptics stock is up 14% to $121.32, a larger climb tied to a fixed cash price replacing a floating share exchange.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $590.75, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $752.16, up 1.36%. That gap shows how much of the move traces to the deal itself.
Under an amended merger agreement, On Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, replacing the all-stock structure. The amendment followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party.
On Semiconductor now expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share upon closing. CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated: “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration.” Funding comes from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing.
Dilution Fades for On Semiconductor, Certainty Arrives for Synaptics
For On Semiconductor shareholders, the core change is the removal of dilution. Paying cash leaves the share count untouched, protecting buyback work that included $332 million of repurchases in Q2 2026.
A fixed cash price gives Synaptics investors certainty, and the Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
Synaptics also brings growth. Its management expects fiscal 2026 Core Internet of Things (IoT) revenue to grow more than 40% to over $385 million, driven by Edge AI and Physical AI design wins. On Semiconductor management stated on the August 3 earnings call that Synaptics’ “market-leading connected compute capabilities” complement On Semiconductor’s “strength in power, sensing, and control.”
The trade-off is debt. Cash and short-term investments totaled $3.9 billion at the end of Q2, with total liquidity of $5.4 billion. Quarterly free cash flow reached $425 million, a support for paying down new borrowing.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the deal, but other jurisdictions are still reviewing it, and Synaptics shareholders must vote. On August 3, On Semiconductor expected the transaction to close in mid-2027.
Investors can watch for the Synaptics stockholder vote and remaining reviews in other jurisdictions before On Semiconductor closes the purchase, as details on the committed debt financing cost could shape how the market judges On Semiconductor’s balance sheet.
Immediate accretion and an AI data center business where management expects revenue to more than double in 2026 support the optimistic view (we covered seven suppliers riding that same AI infrastructure expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). Risks center on new leverage and integrating Synaptics.
Synaptics shareholders now face an outcome fixed at the $123 cash price. Traders may watch whether On Semiconductor stock holds its gains as borrowing terms become clearer.

ON Semiconductor (ON) Switches to $5.7B All-Cash Synaptics Acquisition, Stock Jumps 6%
By Trader EdgeOctober 2, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
ON Semiconductor restructured its Synaptics acquisition into an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $5.7 billion, reduced from the initial $7 billion stock-based proposal.
Synaptics shareholders will receive $123 cash per share rather than the previously agreed 1.350 ON shares from the June announcement.
ON stock surged approximately 6% during premarket hours, while Synaptics shares climbed roughly 14%.
The restructured agreement eliminates shareholder dilution concerns for ON investors and promises immediate accretion to non-GAAP earnings.
Completion of the transaction requires Synaptics shareholder approval and regulatory clearances, with an expected closing date in mid-2027.
Shares of ON Semiconductor rallied approximately 6% in Friday’s premarket session following the company’s announcement of a restructured takeover agreement with Synaptics. The stock had ended Thursday’s session at $80.08.
Synaptics shares posted even stronger gains, climbing approximately 14% on the announcement. Both semiconductor companies specialize in chip technologies for automotive, industrial, and Internet of Things applications.
The initial agreement, announced in June, proposed an all-stock merger structure. Under those terms, Synaptics shareholders would have exchanged each share for 1.350 ON Semiconductor shares, establishing a transaction value near $7 billion.
The revised agreement converts the transaction to an all-cash purchase. Synaptics shareholders will now receive $123 in cash per share, reducing the total transaction value to approximately $5.7 billion.
The price reduction followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from an unnamed third party. Rather than triggering a competitive bidding situation that elevated the acquisition price, the development prompted both parties to negotiate modified terms more favorable to each company.
ON shareholders sidestep the equity dilution that would have resulted from issuing new shares under the original agreement. This change eliminates a significant concern that had pressured the stock since the June announcement.
The company indicates the restructured transaction will immediately enhance its non-GAAP earnings per share. This represents a meaningful improvement from the original structure, which wasn’t projected to be immediately accretive to earnings.
ON had previously identified $200 million in annual cost synergies from the combination. The company now anticipates additional opportunities, including potential revenue synergies and internalizing certain Synaptics manufacturing operations.
The transaction will be funded through a combination of existing cash reserves and debt financing arranged by Morgan Stanley. The absence of a financing contingency for closing eliminates another potential risk factor.
Synaptics CEO Rahul Patel characterized the cash structure as delivering certainty to investors. “We are providing value certainty at a premium as compared to current value,” he said.
The revised terms present a clear tradeoff. Synaptics shareholders forfeit potential participation in the merged entity’s future performance, receiving instead a guaranteed cash payment.
Robert W. Baird analyst Tristan Gerra maintained a Hold rating on ON stock following the announcement, keeping his $108 price target. The broader Wall Street consensus rates ON a Moderate Buy, while Synaptics carries a Hold rating.
Market timing also worked in the company’s favor. Micron’s impressive earnings results released the previous evening had already elevated semiconductor stocks broadly, providing additional momentum for ON’s announcement heading into Friday’s opening.
Treasury yields retreated from recent peaks that same morning, relieving some pressure on growth-oriented technology stocks.
The acquisition still requires approval from Synaptics shareholders alongside regulatory clearances. While the FTC has already granted approval, reviews in additional jurisdictions remain pending.
The companies are targeting a mid-2027 closing timeline. Between now and then, both stocks will likely respond to progress updates on the approval process.

ON Semiconductor's revised Synaptics deal improves earnings outlook, says BofA
ON Semiconductor’s revised $5.7 billion acquisition of Synaptics could deliver a bigger earnings boost than originally expected while eliminating the share dilution that had weighed on the deal, Bank of America said.
Following an unsolicited competing proposal, the companies amended their June 25 agreement to replace the all-stock transaction with a $123-per-share cash offer.
The deal's aggregate value falls to approximately $5.7 billion from $7 billion, eliminating roughly 59 million additional shares and the previously contemplated 12% to 13% dilution.
With ON Semiconductor shares down 32% since the deal's announcement, Bank of America wrote that revised terms could improve investor reception by removing dilution while preserving the strategic rationale.
ON Semiconductor would fund the deal with cash on hand and approximately $2.5 billion in term loan debt, with no financing condition.
Even with that borrowing, the broker estimates the transaction could increase earnings per share by approximately 11% in calendar 2027 and 15% in calendar 2028.
Its combined-company EPS estimates are $5 and $6.88, respectively, compared with standalone forecasts of $4.51 and $5.99.
Those projected gains reflect an estimated 4% dilution and 2% accretion under the original structure, primarily from eliminating additional shares.
The revised model includes cost synergies of $90 million and $175 million, respectively, partly offset by a roughly $150 million annual financial-income headwind from cash-and-debt funding.
The estimates exclude revenue synergies and potential outsourcing benefits beyond the previously announced $200 million annual cost-synergy target, and management expects to outsource some SYNA production after the first 18 months following closing.
The acquisition would also broaden ON Semiconductor's portfolio, with Bank of America highlighting SYNA's edge computing, connectivity, software, and human-machine interfaces alongside existing power and sensing capabilities.
The broker expects the combination to support more integrated solutions across industrial markets, robotics, autonomous driving, and augmented and virtual reality.
It estimates the acquisition would expand ON Semiconductor's calendar 2030 addressable market by approximately $30 billion to $243 billion.
Bank of America still expects completion by mid-2027, with FTC approval received and other regulatory reviews ongoing.

onsemi is reworking its Synaptics deal as a $5.7 billion cash purchase after a rival bid
The amended agreement values Synaptics at $123 per share, down from roughly $7 billion under the original all-stock terms
By Cris Tolomia·2 min read·Updated October 2, 2026
onsemi amended its agreement to acquire Synaptics on Thursday, switching from an all-stock deal to an all-cash purchase of $123 per share, for a total of approximately $5.7 billion. The revision follows an unsolicited competing bid for Synaptics from an unidentified third party.
Under the original June 25, 2026, agreement, onsemi had agreed to exchange 1.35 of its own shares for every Synaptics share, putting the deal's total worth at around $7 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal. At the time of that announcement onsemi's stock was trading at $118.74, but it had slid to roughly $80 a share by the time the revised terms were struck, the Journal reported.
onsemi will finance the transaction through a combination of cash on hand and committed debt. The company said it secured a fully committed senior secured term loan of up to $2.45 billion from Morgan Stanley $MS. The amended agreement removes any closing condition tied to onsemi's financing.
"The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration, and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing," onsemi President and CEO Hassane El-Khoury said in a statement. El-Khoury also pointed to newly identified upside in revenue synergies and insourcing that goes beyond the $200 million in annual run-rate synergies the companies had previously announced, though those gains are not expected to be realized until more than 18 months after the deal closes.
The Synaptics board voted unanimously to support the revised terms. "By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value," Synaptics President and CEO Rahul Patel said in a statement.
Another change under the revised terms is that onsemi is no longer obligated to add a Synaptics director to its board, according to the Journal.
The deal has already received clearance from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, the company said. Regulatory reviews in other jurisdictions remain ongoing. The transaction still requires approval from Synaptics shareholders and is expected to close by mid-2027.
Synaptics stock surged 16% to $122.85 in after-hours trading Thursday. onsemi stock rose 6.9% to $85.57.

NEW YORK — ON Semiconductor shares rose Friday after the chipmaker replaced an all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics with a smaller all-cash bid, a cut in headline price that investors treated as a better deal for the buyer.
The stock traded at $84.94, up $4.85, or 6.06 percent, in morning dealings. Other screens showed the shares as high as about $86, up roughly 8 percent. Synaptics jumped more sharply, about 14 percent, to around $121, just under the new offer price.
Under the amended merger agreement, ON Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, a transaction valued at about $5.7 billion. The June deal had been all stock and had valued Synaptics at about $7 billion. The revision followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party. The Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
"As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders," ON Semiconductor Chief Executive Hassane El-Khoury said in a statement. He also said the all-cash structure "delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration."
The company said it expects the deal to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share at closing. Funding is to come from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing. Reports put committed financing near $2.45 billion. Completion is targeted for mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder approval and customary regulatory clearances.

The arithmetic explains the split reaction. Synaptics holders get a fixed cash price instead of ON shares whose value had fallen. ON Semiconductor stock is down about a third from its midsummer highs, which had shrunk the implied value of the original stock offer and raised doubt that the June terms would hold. Paying cash at $5.7 billion instead of issuing stock at a $7 billion valuation removes dilution and lowers the consideration, which is why the buyer's shares rose on a smaller bid.
Synaptics is an Internet-of-things and interface company whose sensing chips sit at the edge of devices rather than in the data-center processors that have led the semiconductor rally. Management has said it expects fiscal 2026 core IoT revenue to grow more than 40 percent, to more than $385 million, on Edge AI and physical-AI design wins. For ON Semiconductor, the point of the deal is to add that sensing and interface layer to a portfolio built on power devices, including silicon carbide, sold into cars, factories and, increasingly, artificial-intelligence power systems.
That strategy was the subject of the company's investor day. El-Khoury has said that as AI, electrification and automation expand, power density "has emerged as one of the key engineering challenges that will define the next decade," and that the ability to supply power, sense the environment and support decisions "will determine the next generation of intelligent devices." The company has projected a total effective market across automotive, industrial, AI data centers and next-generation uses of $213 billion by 2030. It has also said the AI data-center piece of its business is set to more than double in 2026 and double again in 2027.
Friday's move sits on top of an already strong week. ON Semiconductor closed Thursday at $80.08, up 4.18 percent, before the cash-deal details fully reset the tape. The Friday gain is the market pricing the revised merger, not a second earnings surprise.
Risks remain the ordinary ones in a cash acquisition announced after a competing approach. A higher bid from the unnamed third party could reopen the price. Regulators still have to clear a combination of power semiconductors and edge-sensing chips. Debt taken on to fund $123 a share will sit on a balance sheet that investors had not been asked to lever for this deal in June. And "immediately accretive" is an adjusted figure that excludes the costs of getting there.
For Synaptics holders, the trade is simpler. A stock deal whose value drifted with ON's share price has become a cash bid within a few dollars of where the stock now trades. The board's unanimous support and the premium to the undisturbed price are why SYNA outperformed the buyer on the day.
For ON Semiconductor holders, the gain is a vote that $5.7 billion in cash is preferable to $7 billion in stock for a business meant to extend the company from power into sensing. El-Khoury's case is that the strategic fit has not changed and the terms have improved. The share price on Friday said the market agreed, at least for a morning.

What Happened?
Shares of analog chips maker onsemi (NASDAQ:ON) jumped 5.5% in the morning session after optimism improved, with the stock extending gains from the previous session as the company announced a revised merger agreement to acquire Synaptics Incorporated for $123 per share in cash, lowering the total transaction value to approximately $5.7 billion from approximately $7 billion previously.
The revision came after an unsolicited competing proposal from a third party for Synaptics. Under the amended terms, onsemi stated that the transaction will provide immediate accretion to its non-GAAP earnings per share. According to the company, the transaction will be funded using cash on hand as well as fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley, without any financing closing conditions. The company also confirmed that the amended transaction has received regulatory clearance from the United States Federal Trade Commission. The acquisition is expected to close by mid-2027, subject to customary closing conditions and approval from Synaptics shareholders.
After the initial pop, the shares cooled down to $83.48, up 4.2% from the previous close.

onsemi's shares are extremely volatile and have had 39 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

In a note to clients, Bank of America raised its AMD price target to $720 from $620, projecting agentic workloads will broaden compute needs across server processors. Meta, however, has not named specific chipmakers as contracted infrastructure suppliers.Separately, President Donald Trump announced a productive summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, with high-level talks spotlighting artificial intelligence, according to Bloomberg.Broader equity markets held steady following the announcement, reflecting investor reassurance over diplomatic engagement between the world's two largest economies, Bloomberg reported. Artificial intelligence has become a focal point of global economic competition, making bilateral discussions between Washington and Beijing especially consequential for the technology sector. Constructive engagement between the two nations helps ease investor concerns regarding potential trade friction, supply chain disruptions, or abrupt regulatory restrictions affecting semiconductor and software industries. A stabilized geopolitical backdrop offers greater predictability for multinational technology enterprises investing heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure and cross-border commercial opportunities.
onsemi is up 47.2% since the beginning of the year, but at $83.48 per share, it is still trading 37.7% below its 52-week high of $133.93 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of onsemi's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,860.

ON Semiconductor (ISIN US6821891035) raised its long-term revenue growth target to 12% to 14% annually through 2030 from 10% to 12%. Druckfin reported on September 16, 2026 that management also modeled revenue of USD 11.00 billion by 2030 and retained a 53.00 percent gross-margin target. The larger ambition puts execution and margin delivery at the center of the stock story.
ON Semiconductor's second-quarter 2026 revenue was USD 1.60 billion, up 9.20 percent year over year, while adjusted earnings per share reached USD 0.74 against a USD 0.72 consensus estimate. MarketBeat said on September 29, 2026 that revenue exceeded the USD 1.59 billion forecast and that third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share guidance was USD 0.81 to USD 0.93.
The comparison is important because the growth target is forward-looking, while the latest reported quarter already delivered a 9.20 percent revenue increase. Management's third-quarter guidance therefore gives investors a nearer-term test of whether higher factory utilization can translate into stronger profitability.
Stifel lowered its price target for ON Semiconductor from USD 90.00 to USD 75.00 and kept a Hold rating after the September 16, 2026 analyst day. Investing.com reported that the firm viewed the 12% to 14% revenue compound annual growth target, 53.00 percent gross margin target and 38.00 percent operating-margin target as potentially below expectations.
The split between a higher corporate growth ambition and a lower analyst target creates a clear valuation tension. The market must ultimately judge whether the planned growth rate can produce the margin expansion embedded in the 2030 framework.
ON Semiconductor had a market capitalization of USD 29.9 billion as of September 30, 2026. Its 52-week range was USD 44.56 to USD 134.92, placing the latest primary-market quote of USD 76.87 materially below the yearly high while keeping the stock above its yearly low.

Prediction: ON Semiconductor Could Be a Sleeper AI Infrastructure Winner
Wall Street still prices ON Semiconductor like a cyclical auto chipmaker, but something quietly shifted inside its data centers that the broader market has not yet noticed.
Published September 27, 2026, 1:30pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.

An advanced AI chip, like those driving the industry, symbolizes the crucial role companies like AMD play in the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence landscape. © HelloRF Zcool / Shutterstock.com
Our 24/7 Wall St. price target for ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) is $95.90 over the next 12 months. That points to 24.23% upside from the current $77.20 share price.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
onsemi gets a buy rating in our model because the market still prices it like a cyclical automotive chipmaker, while management expects its AI data center business to more than double in 2026. That gap is the opportunity.
A 10% Weekly Rally Brings the AI Power Story Back
Shares rose 10.32% over the past week and 42.57% year to date. It trades 42.8% below its 52-week high of $134.92 and 73.2% above its low of $44.56.
In its second-quarter earnings report, non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 beat estimates of $0.7153. Revenue of $1.6035 billion also came in ahead of expectations and rose 9.18% year over year. Free cash flow jumped 300.94% to $425.4 million. Third-quarter guidance calls for EPS of $0.81 to $0.93.
Management puts AI data center content at roughly $15,000 per rack today and sees it rising to about $115,000 as racks shift to 800-volt DC power. Silicon carbide revenue from AI data centers should grow nearly 60% in 2026. Recent wins include a bigger role in NVIDIA’s MGX ecosystem and design wins for AWS power supply and battery backup systems.
Lead times extended from 27 weeks to 32 weeks, and utilization rose to 83%. Each utilization point adds 25 to 30 basis points of gross margin.
For 2027, the high analyst EPS estimate is $5.3992. Of analysts covering the stock, 13 rate it a buy or strong buy and none rate it a sell. Our bull case target is $119.44.
Revenue in the Analog and Mixed-Signal Group fell 2% year over year. When Barclays initiated coverage, it set an equal-weight rating and a $75 target, citing heavy exposure to automotive and China. Restructuring charges of $329.3 million in the first quarter weighed on GAAP results.
Those charges fund a leaner manufacturing operations, which should yield about $35 million in annualized savings. Other risks include possible dilution from convertible notes and integrating the Synaptics acquisition. Buybacks are also running at about 105% of free cash flow. The bear case target is $79.16.
ON Trades at a Deep Discount to TI and Analog Devices
Texas Instruments (NASDAQ:TXN) sells analog and power chips into industrial, automotive and data center markets. Its second-quarter revenue grew 22.82%.
Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI) acquired Empower Semiconductor for AI server power. Revenue rose 39.63% with adjusted operating margin of 50.0%. ON’s lower margins explain part of the discount. Our target works out to about 21x the 2027 consensus EPS of $4.5288, below both peers’ forward multiples.
ON Semiconductor Price Prediction 2026-2030
The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $95.90 carries a buy rating with 90% confidence. AI data center growth coming while ON trades at a steep discount to peers tips the scale.
The case improves if gross margin reaches the forecast 40% to 42% range. I would grow cautious if automotive demand in China fades.

These projections assume onsemi keeps implementing its existing strategy. The results could land well above or below them depending on how fast 800-volt data center power is adopted and how the Synaptics integration goes.
