On Semiconductor Climbs 8%, Synaptics Surges 14% as $5.7B Cash Bid Replaces $7B Stock Deal
On Semiconductor scrapped its stock deal for Synaptics and replaced it with cash, and both stocks surged on the news for reasons that point in opposite directions.
Published October 2, 2026, 9:13am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A revised takeover agreement is lifting both the buyer and the target in a chip deal that just got simpler. On Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) stock is at $86.64, up 8% in morning trading. This follows the company replacing its $7 billion all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) with a $5.7 billion all-cash bid.
Synaptics stock is up 14% to $121.32, a larger climb tied to a fixed cash price replacing a floating share exchange.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $590.75, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $752.16, up 1.36%. That gap shows how much of the move traces to the deal itself.
Under an amended merger agreement, On Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, replacing the all-stock structure. The amendment followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party.
On Semiconductor now expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share upon closing. CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated: “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration.” Funding comes from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing.
Dilution Fades for On Semiconductor, Certainty Arrives for Synaptics
For On Semiconductor shareholders, the core change is the removal of dilution. Paying cash leaves the share count untouched, protecting buyback work that included $332 million of repurchases in Q2 2026.
A fixed cash price gives Synaptics investors certainty, and the Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
Synaptics also brings growth. Its management expects fiscal 2026 Core Internet of Things (IoT) revenue to grow more than 40% to over $385 million, driven by Edge AI and Physical AI design wins. On Semiconductor management stated on the August 3 earnings call that Synaptics’ “market-leading connected compute capabilities” complement On Semiconductor’s “strength in power, sensing, and control.”
The trade-off is debt. Cash and short-term investments totaled $3.9 billion at the end of Q2, with total liquidity of $5.4 billion. Quarterly free cash flow reached $425 million, a support for paying down new borrowing.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the deal, but other jurisdictions are still reviewing it, and Synaptics shareholders must vote. On August 3, On Semiconductor expected the transaction to close in mid-2027.
Investors can watch for the Synaptics stockholder vote and remaining reviews in other jurisdictions before On Semiconductor closes the purchase, as details on the committed debt financing cost could shape how the market judges On Semiconductor’s balance sheet.
Immediate accretion and an AI data center business where management expects revenue to more than double in 2026 support the optimistic view (we covered seven suppliers riding that same AI infrastructure expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). Risks center on new leverage and integrating Synaptics.
Synaptics shareholders now face an outcome fixed at the $123 cash price. Traders may watch whether On Semiconductor stock holds its gains as borrowing terms become clearer.

ON Semiconductor (ON) Switches to $5.7B All-Cash Synaptics Acquisition, Stock Jumps 6%
By Trader EdgeOctober 2, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
ON Semiconductor restructured its Synaptics acquisition into an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $5.7 billion, reduced from the initial $7 billion stock-based proposal.
Synaptics shareholders will receive $123 cash per share rather than the previously agreed 1.350 ON shares from the June announcement.
ON stock surged approximately 6% during premarket hours, while Synaptics shares climbed roughly 14%.
The restructured agreement eliminates shareholder dilution concerns for ON investors and promises immediate accretion to non-GAAP earnings.
Completion of the transaction requires Synaptics shareholder approval and regulatory clearances, with an expected closing date in mid-2027.
Shares of ON Semiconductor rallied approximately 6% in Friday’s premarket session following the company’s announcement of a restructured takeover agreement with Synaptics. The stock had ended Thursday’s session at $80.08.
Synaptics shares posted even stronger gains, climbing approximately 14% on the announcement. Both semiconductor companies specialize in chip technologies for automotive, industrial, and Internet of Things applications.
The initial agreement, announced in June, proposed an all-stock merger structure. Under those terms, Synaptics shareholders would have exchanged each share for 1.350 ON Semiconductor shares, establishing a transaction value near $7 billion.
The revised agreement converts the transaction to an all-cash purchase. Synaptics shareholders will now receive $123 in cash per share, reducing the total transaction value to approximately $5.7 billion.
The price reduction followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from an unnamed third party. Rather than triggering a competitive bidding situation that elevated the acquisition price, the development prompted both parties to negotiate modified terms more favorable to each company.
ON shareholders sidestep the equity dilution that would have resulted from issuing new shares under the original agreement. This change eliminates a significant concern that had pressured the stock since the June announcement.
The company indicates the restructured transaction will immediately enhance its non-GAAP earnings per share. This represents a meaningful improvement from the original structure, which wasn’t projected to be immediately accretive to earnings.
ON had previously identified $200 million in annual cost synergies from the combination. The company now anticipates additional opportunities, including potential revenue synergies and internalizing certain Synaptics manufacturing operations.
The transaction will be funded through a combination of existing cash reserves and debt financing arranged by Morgan Stanley. The absence of a financing contingency for closing eliminates another potential risk factor.
Synaptics CEO Rahul Patel characterized the cash structure as delivering certainty to investors. “We are providing value certainty at a premium as compared to current value,” he said.
The revised terms present a clear tradeoff. Synaptics shareholders forfeit potential participation in the merged entity’s future performance, receiving instead a guaranteed cash payment.
Robert W. Baird analyst Tristan Gerra maintained a Hold rating on ON stock following the announcement, keeping his $108 price target. The broader Wall Street consensus rates ON a Moderate Buy, while Synaptics carries a Hold rating.
Market timing also worked in the company’s favor. Micron’s impressive earnings results released the previous evening had already elevated semiconductor stocks broadly, providing additional momentum for ON’s announcement heading into Friday’s opening.
Treasury yields retreated from recent peaks that same morning, relieving some pressure on growth-oriented technology stocks.
The acquisition still requires approval from Synaptics shareholders alongside regulatory clearances. While the FTC has already granted approval, reviews in additional jurisdictions remain pending.
The companies are targeting a mid-2027 closing timeline. Between now and then, both stocks will likely respond to progress updates on the approval process.

ON Semiconductor's revised Synaptics deal improves earnings outlook, says BofA
ON Semiconductor’s revised $5.7 billion acquisition of Synaptics could deliver a bigger earnings boost than originally expected while eliminating the share dilution that had weighed on the deal, Bank of America said.
Following an unsolicited competing proposal, the companies amended their June 25 agreement to replace the all-stock transaction with a $123-per-share cash offer.
The deal's aggregate value falls to approximately $5.7 billion from $7 billion, eliminating roughly 59 million additional shares and the previously contemplated 12% to 13% dilution.
With ON Semiconductor shares down 32% since the deal's announcement, Bank of America wrote that revised terms could improve investor reception by removing dilution while preserving the strategic rationale.
ON Semiconductor would fund the deal with cash on hand and approximately $2.5 billion in term loan debt, with no financing condition.
Even with that borrowing, the broker estimates the transaction could increase earnings per share by approximately 11% in calendar 2027 and 15% in calendar 2028.
Its combined-company EPS estimates are $5 and $6.88, respectively, compared with standalone forecasts of $4.51 and $5.99.
Those projected gains reflect an estimated 4% dilution and 2% accretion under the original structure, primarily from eliminating additional shares.
The revised model includes cost synergies of $90 million and $175 million, respectively, partly offset by a roughly $150 million annual financial-income headwind from cash-and-debt funding.
The estimates exclude revenue synergies and potential outsourcing benefits beyond the previously announced $200 million annual cost-synergy target, and management expects to outsource some SYNA production after the first 18 months following closing.
The acquisition would also broaden ON Semiconductor's portfolio, with Bank of America highlighting SYNA's edge computing, connectivity, software, and human-machine interfaces alongside existing power and sensing capabilities.
The broker expects the combination to support more integrated solutions across industrial markets, robotics, autonomous driving, and augmented and virtual reality.
It estimates the acquisition would expand ON Semiconductor's calendar 2030 addressable market by approximately $30 billion to $243 billion.
Bank of America still expects completion by mid-2027, with FTC approval received and other regulatory reviews ongoing.

onsemi is reworking its Synaptics deal as a $5.7 billion cash purchase after a rival bid
The amended agreement values Synaptics at $123 per share, down from roughly $7 billion under the original all-stock terms
By Cris Tolomia·2 min read·Updated October 2, 2026
onsemi amended its agreement to acquire Synaptics on Thursday, switching from an all-stock deal to an all-cash purchase of $123 per share, for a total of approximately $5.7 billion. The revision follows an unsolicited competing bid for Synaptics from an unidentified third party.
Under the original June 25, 2026, agreement, onsemi had agreed to exchange 1.35 of its own shares for every Synaptics share, putting the deal's total worth at around $7 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal. At the time of that announcement onsemi's stock was trading at $118.74, but it had slid to roughly $80 a share by the time the revised terms were struck, the Journal reported.
onsemi will finance the transaction through a combination of cash on hand and committed debt. The company said it secured a fully committed senior secured term loan of up to $2.45 billion from Morgan Stanley $MS. The amended agreement removes any closing condition tied to onsemi's financing.
"The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration, and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing," onsemi President and CEO Hassane El-Khoury said in a statement. El-Khoury also pointed to newly identified upside in revenue synergies and insourcing that goes beyond the $200 million in annual run-rate synergies the companies had previously announced, though those gains are not expected to be realized until more than 18 months after the deal closes.
The Synaptics board voted unanimously to support the revised terms. "By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value," Synaptics President and CEO Rahul Patel said in a statement.
Another change under the revised terms is that onsemi is no longer obligated to add a Synaptics director to its board, according to the Journal.
The deal has already received clearance from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, the company said. Regulatory reviews in other jurisdictions remain ongoing. The transaction still requires approval from Synaptics shareholders and is expected to close by mid-2027.
Synaptics stock surged 16% to $122.85 in after-hours trading Thursday. onsemi stock rose 6.9% to $85.57.

pages.text:
NEW YORK — ON Semiconductor shares rose Friday after the chipmaker replaced an all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics with a smaller all-cash bid, a cut in headline price that investors treated as a better deal for the buyer.
The stock traded at $84.94, up $4.85, or 6.06 percent, in morning dealings. Other screens showed the shares as high as about $86, up roughly 8 percent. Synaptics jumped more sharply, about 14 percent, to around $121, just under the new offer price.
Under the amended merger agreement, ON Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, a transaction valued at about $5.7 billion. The June deal had been all stock and had valued Synaptics at about $7 billion. The revision followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party. The Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
"As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders," ON Semiconductor Chief Executive Hassane El-Khoury said in a statement. He also said the all-cash structure "delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration."
The company said it expects the deal to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share at closing. Funding is to come from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing. Reports put committed financing near $2.45 billion. Completion is targeted for mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder approval and customary regulatory clearances.

The arithmetic explains the split reaction. Synaptics holders get a fixed cash price instead of ON shares whose value had fallen. ON Semiconductor stock is down about a third from its midsummer highs, which had shrunk the implied value of the original stock offer and raised doubt that the June terms would hold. Paying cash at $5.7 billion instead of issuing stock at a $7 billion valuation removes dilution and lowers the consideration, which is why the buyer's shares rose on a smaller bid.
Synaptics is an Internet-of-things and interface company whose sensing chips sit at the edge of devices rather than in the data-center processors that have led the semiconductor rally. Management has said it expects fiscal 2026 core IoT revenue to grow more than 40 percent, to more than $385 million, on Edge AI and physical-AI design wins. For ON Semiconductor, the point of the deal is to add that sensing and interface layer to a portfolio built on power devices, including silicon carbide, sold into cars, factories and, increasingly, artificial-intelligence power systems.
That strategy was the subject of the company's investor day. El-Khoury has said that as AI, electrification and automation expand, power density "has emerged as one of the key engineering challenges that will define the next decade," and that the ability to supply power, sense the environment and support decisions "will determine the next generation of intelligent devices." The company has projected a total effective market across automotive, industrial, AI data centers and next-generation uses of $213 billion by 2030. It has also said the AI data-center piece of its business is set to more than double in 2026 and double again in 2027.
Friday's move sits on top of an already strong week. ON Semiconductor closed Thursday at $80.08, up 4.18 percent, before the cash-deal details fully reset the tape. The Friday gain is the market pricing the revised merger, not a second earnings surprise.
Risks remain the ordinary ones in a cash acquisition announced after a competing approach. A higher bid from the unnamed third party could reopen the price. Regulators still have to clear a combination of power semiconductors and edge-sensing chips. Debt taken on to fund $123 a share will sit on a balance sheet that investors had not been asked to lever for this deal in June. And "immediately accretive" is an adjusted figure that excludes the costs of getting there.
For Synaptics holders, the trade is simpler. A stock deal whose value drifted with ON's share price has become a cash bid within a few dollars of where the stock now trades. The board's unanimous support and the premium to the undisturbed price are why SYNA outperformed the buyer on the day.
For ON Semiconductor holders, the gain is a vote that $5.7 billion in cash is preferable to $7 billion in stock for a business meant to extend the company from power into sensing. El-Khoury's case is that the strategic fit has not changed and the terms have improved. The share price on Friday said the market agreed, at least for a morning.

ON Semiconductor (ISIN US6821891035) raised its long-term revenue growth target to 12% to 14% annually through 2030 from 10% to 12%. Druckfin reported on September 16, 2026 that management also modeled revenue of USD 11.00 billion by 2030 and retained a 53.00 percent gross-margin target. The larger ambition puts execution and margin delivery at the center of the stock story.
ON Semiconductor's second-quarter 2026 revenue was USD 1.60 billion, up 9.20 percent year over year, while adjusted earnings per share reached USD 0.74 against a USD 0.72 consensus estimate. MarketBeat said on September 29, 2026 that revenue exceeded the USD 1.59 billion forecast and that third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share guidance was USD 0.81 to USD 0.93.
The comparison is important because the growth target is forward-looking, while the latest reported quarter already delivered a 9.20 percent revenue increase. Management's third-quarter guidance therefore gives investors a nearer-term test of whether higher factory utilization can translate into stronger profitability.
Stifel lowered its price target for ON Semiconductor from USD 90.00 to USD 75.00 and kept a Hold rating after the September 16, 2026 analyst day. Investing.com reported that the firm viewed the 12% to 14% revenue compound annual growth target, 53.00 percent gross margin target and 38.00 percent operating-margin target as potentially below expectations.
The split between a higher corporate growth ambition and a lower analyst target creates a clear valuation tension. The market must ultimately judge whether the planned growth rate can produce the margin expansion embedded in the 2030 framework.
ON Semiconductor had a market capitalization of USD 29.9 billion as of September 30, 2026. Its 52-week range was USD 44.56 to USD 134.92, placing the latest primary-market quote of USD 76.87 materially below the yearly high while keeping the stock above its yearly low.
ON Semiconductor is listed on NASDAQ under ticker ON. The company operates in the Technology sector and Semiconductors industry, supplying power and sensing solutions for automotive, industrial, energy and data-center applications.

Prediction: ON Semiconductor Could Be a Sleeper AI Infrastructure Winner
Wall Street still prices ON Semiconductor like a cyclical auto chipmaker, but something quietly shifted inside its data centers that the broader market has not yet noticed.
Published September 27, 2026, 1:30pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
An advanced AI chip, like those driving the industry, symbolizes the crucial role companies like AMD play in the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence landscape. © HelloRF Zcool / Shutterstock.com
Our 24/7 Wall St. price target for ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) is $95.90 over the next 12 months. That points to 24.23% upside from the current $77.20 share price.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
onsemi gets a buy rating in our model because the market still prices it like a cyclical automotive chipmaker, while management expects its AI data center business to more than double in 2026. That gap is the opportunity.
A 10% Weekly Rally Brings the AI Power Story Back
Shares rose 10.32% over the past week and 42.57% year to date. It trades 42.8% below its 52-week high of $134.92 and 73.2% above its low of $44.56.
In its second-quarter earnings report, non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 beat estimates of $0.7153. Revenue of $1.6035 billion also came in ahead of expectations and rose 9.18% year over year. Free cash flow jumped 300.94% to $425.4 million. Third-quarter guidance calls for EPS of $0.81 to $0.93.
Management puts AI data center content at roughly $15,000 per rack today and sees it rising to about $115,000 as racks shift to 800-volt DC power. Silicon carbide revenue from AI data centers should grow nearly 60% in 2026. Recent wins include a bigger role in NVIDIA’s MGX ecosystem and design wins for AWS power supply and battery backup systems.
Lead times extended from 27 weeks to 32 weeks, and utilization rose to 83%. Each utilization point adds 25 to 30 basis points of gross margin.
For 2027, the high analyst EPS estimate is $5.3992. Of analysts covering the stock, 13 rate it a buy or strong buy and none rate it a sell. Our bull case target is $119.44.
Revenue in the Analog and Mixed-Signal Group fell 2% year over year. When Barclays initiated coverage, it set an equal-weight rating and a $75 target, citing heavy exposure to automotive and China. Restructuring charges of $329.3 million in the first quarter weighed on GAAP results.
Those charges fund a leaner manufacturing operations, which should yield about $35 million in annualized savings. Other risks include possible dilution from convertible notes and integrating the Synaptics acquisition. Buybacks are also running at about 105% of free cash flow. The bear case target is $79.16.
ON Trades at a Deep Discount to TI and Analog Devices
Texas Instruments (NASDAQ:TXN) sells analog and power chips into industrial, automotive and data center markets. Its second-quarter revenue grew 22.82%.
Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI) acquired Empower Semiconductor for AI server power. Revenue rose 39.63% with adjusted operating margin of 50.0%. ON’s lower margins explain part of the discount. Our target works out to about 21x the 2027 consensus EPS of $4.5288, below both peers’ forward multiples.
ON Semiconductor Price Prediction 2026-2030
The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $95.90 carries a buy rating with 90% confidence. AI data center growth coming while ON trades at a steep discount to peers tips the scale.
The case improves if gross margin reaches the forecast 40% to 42% range. I would grow cautious if automotive demand in China fades.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
These projections assume onsemi keeps implementing its existing strategy. The results could land well above or below them depending on how fast 800-volt data center power is adopted and how the Synaptics integration goes.

ON Semiconductor stock (ISIN US6821891035) closed at USD 66.60 on the Nasdaq on September 16, 2026, down 9.0 percent from the prior session and extending a multi-week slide for the chipmaker as investors digested fresh guidance and analyst commentary around its long-term growth strategy.
Investor Day triggers sharp single-day drop
According to an article from Ad-hoc-news.de on September 17, 2026, ON Semiconductor stock fell from an opening level around USD 74.42 to a close at USD 66.60 on September 16, 2026, erasing roughly USD 2 billion in market value and marking an unusually large daily swing for the name.
The same report cites data from Investing.com and 24/7 Wall St. showing that during the September 16, 2026 session the shares traded between an intraday high near USD 74.42 and a low around USD 66.50, underperforming broader semiconductor indices that were roughly flat to modestly higher on the day.
As Tickeron reported on September 17, 2026, the September 16 Investor Day became the biggest catalyst in the past month, with the stock dropping about 9 percent in that single session and contributing to a roughly 16 percent decline over the prior 30 days from around USD 79.42 on August 18, 2026 to USD 66.60 by the September 16, 2026 close.
Long-term targets and Q2 2026 fundamentals
At its Investor Day on September 16, 2026, ON Semiconductor outlined a long-term growth strategy focused on power solutions for AI, electrification and automation, including an updated revenue ambition for the coming decade. As described by Moomoo on September 17, 2026, the company presented its roadmap to power the next decade of innovation by addressing growing power constraints in AI data centers, electric vehicles and industrial automation.
Alongside the strategy discussion, investors have been weighing the latest quarterly figures. In Q2 2026, reported on August 3, 2026, ON Semiconductor delivered revenue of USD 1.60 billion, which was up 9.2 percent year over year from roughly USD 1.47 billion in the same quarter of 2025 and slightly ahead of the USD 1.59 billion consensus estimate according to MarketBeat.
The same MarketBeat overview notes that earnings per share for Q2 2026 came in at USD 0.74, beating the consensus forecast of USD 0.72 by USD 0.02 and improving from USD 0.53 in the comparable quarter a year earlier, while net margin stood at 10.17 percent and return on equity at 14.06 percent.
Looking ahead, ON Semiconductor has issued guidance for Q3 2026 with expected earnings per share between USD 0.81 and USD 0.93, implying sequential growth from the Q2 2026 level of USD 0.74 and underpinning analyst forecasts that, as summarized by MarketBeat, point to full-year 2026 earnings per share of about USD 3.23.
Analysts recalibrate price targets and ratings
The sharp price reaction around the Investor Day has been accompanied by an active period of analyst updates on ON Semiconductor stock. On September 17, 2026, Needham reiterated a Buy rating on the shares and maintained a price target of USD 116, according to MarketBeat.
A parallel alert from MarketBeat on September 17, 2026 indicates that Cantor Fitzgerald cut its price target on ON Semiconductor from USD 110 to USD 90 while keeping a Neutral rating, aligning its valuation with a multiple of 14 times its calendar year 2028 upside earnings per share estimate versus 17 times previously.
On the same day, MarketBeat reported that Wells Fargo reduced its price target on ON Semiconductor from USD 95 to USD 85 while maintaining an Overweight rating, citing updated assumptions on margins and sector multiples.
As a further data point, Rosenblatt Securities reaffirmed a Neutral rating with a USD 85 price objective, and MarketBeat notes that, based on its compilation of coverage, ON Semiconductor currently carries a consensus rating of Moderate Buy with an average price target of USD 93.36, providing a benchmark against the September 16, 2026 close at USD 66.60.
An analysis from Investing.com on September 17, 2026 highlights that Stifel lowered its price target on ON Semiconductor stock from USD 90 to USD 75 while maintaining a Hold rating, citing margin outlook concerns as a key factor.
The same Investing.com piece notes that Cantor Fitzgerald and Mizuho also reduced their targets, with Cantor moving from USD 110 to USD 90 and Mizuho from USD 110 to USD 95, while retaining Neutral and Outperform ratings respectively, and that Wells Fargo trimmed its forecast to USD 95 from USD 110 with an Overweight stance.
For investors, the divergence between the adjusted price targets in the USD 75 to USD 116 range and the current stock level around USD 66.60 underscores a debate about how quickly ON Semiconductor can translate its power-focused roadmap and silicon carbide content into sustained earnings growth and margin expansion.
Risks mentioned across analyst and media coverage include sensitivity to automotive and industrial demand cycles, execution on AI data center opportunities, and the possibility that higher interest rates or sector-wide valuation compression could further weigh on multiples even if fundamentals remain intact.
ON Semiconductor stock trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker ON. Per Nasdaq price data reflected on a major financial portal, the shares closed at USD 66.60 on September 16, 2026, representing a 9.02 percent decline versus the prior close of USD 73.20, with the session marked by heavy volume relative to recent averages.
The recent drawdown has also pushed the shares well below commonly watched moving averages. A technical snapshot summarized by a stock-news portal indicates that ON Semiconductor was trading about 6.8 percent under its 20-day simple moving average of USD 72.87 and roughly 14.3 percent under its 200-day simple moving average of USD 79.21, with chart resistance near USD 74 and support around USD 55 as of mid-September 2026.
From a medium-term perspective, Tickeron calculates that ON Semiconductor shares have fallen around 44 percent over the past quarter while remaining positive year to date, suggesting that despite the recent volatility, longer-horizon investors still see potential in the company’s positioning in power semiconductors for vehicles and data centers.

ON Semiconductor Has Cratered for 3 Months: This Wall Street Pro Remains Bullish, Citing 120% Returns for Buyers
ON Semiconductor shed nearly half its value in three months while its peers barely flinched, yet one Wall Street analyst just doubled down with the most aggressive price target on the Street. The disconnect between the selloff and the operating…
Published September 18, 2026, 7:25am ET · 4 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
This graphic illustrates the significant 56% gap between ON Semiconductor's current price of $68.30 and the average analyst target of $106.88 as of September 17, 2026. It also details the stock's recent -43.8% drop over three months, contrasting with a largely bullish analyst sentiment. © 24/7 Wall St.
ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) trades at $68.30 after a brutal summer, while the average Wall Street price target sits at $106.88. That leaves the stock roughly 56% below where analysts, on average, think it should trade.
ON is the Phoenix-based designer behind onsemi, a top supplier of intelligent power and sensing chips for cars, factories, and increasingly, AI server racks. Its EliteSiC silicon carbide and GaNEXUS gallium nitride families are pitched as the plumbing for 800-volt vehicle platforms and the next generation of hyperscaler power trees. Wall Street cares because that story sits at the intersection of two of the biggest capex cycles in tech.
Even after a brutal selloff, business metrics are improving and analysts have not wavered. One has doubled down.
A Three-Month Wipeout in a Rallying Market
Shares of ON have plunged 43.84% over the past three months, a decline steep enough to qualify as a full-blown crash. The stock started that window at $121.62 and has bled all the way down to its current level, with a 14% drop just in the last month.
The selloff came despite strong results. Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue of $1.60 billion beat estimates and rose 9.18% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 topping the $0.7153 consensus. Shares popped more than 5% after the report. The unwind has been driven by broader concerns: high automotive exposure, China cyclicality, a rich trailing valuation, and profit-taking after a run that had ON near $134.92 on a 52-week basis. The peer group softened too, but ON fell harder and faster.
Why Susquehanna Still Sees Roughly 120% Upside
Analysts have not chased the stock lower. Coverage sits at 2 Strong Buy, 11 Buy, 16 Hold, and zero Sell ratings, and estimate revisions have skewed sharply higher, with 25 upward EPS revisions for fiscal 2026 in the trailing 30 days against just two down.
Susquehanna’s Christopher Rolland reiterated a Buy with a Street-high $150 price target, implying roughly 120% upside from $68.30. His thesis: EliteSiC capturing dominant share as EV platforms shift from 400V to 800V architectures, AI data center power scaling through smart power stages and point-of-load converters, and gross margins recovering toward 40%+.
Management backs that narrative. AI data center is now expected to more than double in 2026. CEO Hassane El-Khoury told investors, “Our growth in data center is literally from the wall to the core.” Silicon carbide revenue in data centers is guided to grow nearly 60% year over year, with content per rack jumping from $15,000 to $115,000 in an 800-volt DC architecture. Non-GAAP gross margin already expanded to 39.3%, with Q3 guidance calling for 40% to 42%.
Analog Peers Held Up While ON Broke Down
This selloff is largely a single-name story. Peers softened but held ground.
NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) trades at $227.95 against a target of $311.10, roughly 36% of implied upside. NXPI is up 5.02% year to date with 6 Strong Buy, 16 Buy, 7 Hold and 1 Sell ratings, a solidly bullish tilt.
Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI) has been the sector standout, up 33.72% year to date at $362.65 against a $470.72 target, about 30% upside. Coverage skews aggressively bullish at 7 Strong Buy, 24 Buy, 3 Hold.
ON’s analyst-implied upside is the widest in the group. That makes ON the outlier in the group.
ON trades at $68.30 versus a consensus target of $106.88 from 30 covering analysts, implying 56% upside to the average and about 120% to Susquehanna’s $150. The forward P/E of 16 reflects the sharp fiscal 2026 earnings ramp analysts are modeling toward $3.2028 full-year EPS.
ON is up 26.13% year to date, ahead of the S&P 500‘s 11.85%, but that lead was built and lost in a violent round trip. Over three months, ON’s 43.84% drawdown stands in stark contrast to a flat-to-up broad market.
The bull case for ON here rests on the AI data center ramp and silicon carbide share gains materializing over the next few quarters. Q3 guidance already points to gross margins of 40% to 42%, book-to-bill has been above 1 for several quarters, and lead times have extended to roughly 32 weeks. Deliver on those numbers and even the consensus $106.88 becomes conservative.
The bear case centers on automotive weakness in Europe, China exposure, and the pending Synaptics acquisition integration risk are what the market is pricing in. A stalled industrial recovery or a slip in AI content per rack could keep the multiple compressed.
My lean is cautiously bullish. The analyst dispersion is wide for a reason, but the operating data is moving in the bulls’ direction, and ON’s dislocation looks larger than the fundamentals justify.

Onsemi (ON) will now buy Synaptics (SYNA) for $123 a share in cash for about $5.7 billion under a revised agreement, the firms said. Meta Platforms (META) is facing up to $40 billion in penalties after a US jury found that the company misled consumers over data privacy on Facebook in relation with the Cambridge Analytica scandal, Reuters reported. Shares were up 0.4%.

onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement
Revised Terms to Deliver Higher onsemi Shareholder Value through Immediate EPS Accretion
Amended Agreement Follows Thorough Review of Unsolicited Competing Proposal
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. and SAN JOSE, Calif. – Oct. 1, 2026 – onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) and Synaptics Incorporated (NASDAQ: SYNA) ("Synaptics") today announced they have amended
their June 25, 2026 merger agreement. The amendment follows an unsolicited competing proposal received from a third party.
Under the revised agreement, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in cash for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion as compared to approximately $7
billion for the prior agreement. The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to onsemi’s non-GAAP earnings per share and provides value certainty for Synaptics’ shareholders.
“As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger
agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration,
and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing. In addition, we have identified incremental opportunities to create shareholder value beyond the previously announced $200 million of annual run-rate
synergies. These additional benefits from revenue synergies and insourcing of a portion of Synaptics’ production are expected to be realized after the initial 18 months
post-close, further strengthening the long-term earnings and cash flow profile of the combined company.”
El-Khoury continued, “Synaptics is accretive to our long-term model, with a strong growth outlook and attractive gross margin profile that will help accelerate onsemi’s
evolution. Additionally, Synaptics complements growth in our AI data center business, and brings to onsemi its highly profitable human-machine interface, and sensing products businesses that generate strong and predictable cash flows, providing the
combined company with a durable funding engine to accelerate its connected compute capabilities.”
After careful review with its financial and legal advisors, the Synaptics Board unanimously determined that the onsemi transaction, as amended, continues to be in the
best interests of Synaptics and its shareholders.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," said Rahul Patel,
Synaptics President and CEO. “By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders."
The transaction will be financed through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing. onsemi has obtained fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley.
The amended merger agreement does not include a closing condition related to onsemi’s financing.
The transaction is still expected to close by mid-2027, subject to approval by Synaptics shareholders, the receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary
closing conditions. The transaction has been approved by the United States Federal Trade Commission, and regulators in other jurisdictions are reviewing the transaction.
More Information:
Investor Presentation: onsemi & Synaptics Revised Merger Terms1
onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) delivers intelligent power and sensing technologies that enable electrification, energy efficiency, safety, and automation across automotive,
industrial, and AI data center end‑markets. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi helps customers solve complex challenges to achieve higher efficiency, improved performance, and lower system cost, while supporting a
safer, cleaner, and more energy‑efficient world. The company is part of the S&P 500® index. Learn more at www.onsemi.com.
Synaptics (Nasdaq: SYNA) is driving innovation in AI at the Edge, bringing AI closer to end users and transforming how we engage with intelligent connected devices,
whether at home, at work, or on the move. As a go-to partner for forward-thinking product innovators, Synaptics powers the future with its cutting-edge Synaptics Astra™ AI-Native embedded compute, wireless connectivity, and multimodal sensing
solutions. We’re making the digital experience smarter, faster, more intuitive, secure, and seamless. From touch, display, and biometrics to AI-driven wireless connectivity, video, vision, audio, speech, and security processing, Synaptics is a
force behind the next generation of technology enhancing how we live, work, and play.
Vice President - Investor Relations & Corporate Development

Ciena (CIEN) closed the last trading session at $379.14, gaining 19.4% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $518.74 indicates a 36.8% upside potential.

While the lowest estimate of $347.00 indicates a 8.5% decline from the current price level, the most optimistic analyst expects the stock to surge 74.1% to reach $660.00. It's very important to note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.
But, for CIEN, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.
Zacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for CIEN
Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 10.7%, as nine estimates have moved higher compared to no negative revision.
Moreover, CIEN currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), which means it is in the top 5% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much CIEN could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

Bullish analyst calls piled up all week on one optical networking name, and now the stock is surging while its closest peers barely budge. Here is what the sell-side sees that the market is only starting to price in.
Published October 1, 2026, 11:57am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A week of upbeat sell-side research on artificial intelligence (AI) networking is showing up in shares of Ciena (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction). Ciena stock is at $371.68, up 6% in early trading action. With the company itself quiet on news, the gain looks like the market catching up to a sell-side re-rating of Ciena stock that’s been building for a week.
Meanwhile, shares of fellow AI networking supplier Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) are at $205.30, up 0.8%. Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) stock is holding steady at $107.94, up 0.3%. That split leaves Ciena stock out in front of the networking group by a wide margin.
Tech names are stronger overall, with the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) at $265.36, up 0.2%. In contrast, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is at $760.92, down 0.2%.
Evercore and Bernstein Make the Optical Case
Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani upgraded Ciena stock to Outperform late last week and raised the firm’s price target to $550. Daryanani’s argument is that an AI system runs only as fast as the chips inside it can exchange information across server racks and between data centers. When those connections fall behind, operators lose efficiency. They struggle to get full use of equipment they’ve already paid for, and Daryanani sees the opportunity in Ciena’s optical networking technology, which moves that traffic inside data centers and over longer distances.
Bernstein added to the momentum in the previous session, launching coverage of Ciena stock at Outperform as part of a positive rollout across the U.S. networking group. In that research, Bernstein told investors that networking and optical companies stand to be structural winners within AI infrastructure. Both calls point at the same bottleneck, and Ciena sells the optical transport that lets data centers, and the links between them, keep pace with the compute being installed around them.
Ciena’s Own Re-Rating Stands Apart From Its Peers
Ciena stock is up 59% year to date, so the two analyst calls are landing on a name that has already run a long way. Evercore ISI’s higher price target arriving after that kind of climb raises the bar into strength, at a point when the market was already rewarding Ciena’s optical franchise.
Arista and Cisco shares are barely moving alongside Ciena stock, suggesting the market views the analyst calls as specific to Ciena. Extreme Networks (NASDAQ:EXTR), a smaller enterprise networking peer, rounds out the group.
Both firms point to a bottleneck supporting the bullish thesis, where every new rack of AI chips depends on faster optical links (we highlighted seven suppliers solving exactly these AI expansion bottlenecks, from power to networking, in a free report here). Much of that story may already be priced in after this year’s run, so any slowdown in AI infrastructure spending could weigh on the shares.
It’s worth watching whether other firms follow Evercore ISI and Bernstein with bullish research on Ciena. Any pickup in Arista or Cisco shares toward Ciena’s pace could signal the buying is spreading across AI networking.
Anyone sizing up their exposure should adjust their holdings carefully given that Ciena stock is up 59% year to date and the latest price target raise arrived into strength. Keeping one’s Ciena stake moderate leaves room to benefit from the AI networking demand case both firms laid out while limiting the damage if momentum in CIEN stock fades.

Ciena’s Earnings Call Highlights AI-Fueled Growth Wave
Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Sep 16, 7:06PM CDT
Ciena Corporation ((CIEN)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Ciena Corporation delivered a confident and upbeat earnings call, underscoring record revenue, margins, and EPS alongside surging orders and backlog. Management framed the quarter as evidence of a durable, AI-driven upcycle, while acknowledging supply constraints, higher near-term cash investments, and tariff uncertainties that may temper the pace, but not the trajectory, of growth.
Record Revenue and Profitability Break New Ground
Ciena posted Q3 revenue of $1.67 billion, a 37% year-on-year jump and another all-time quarterly high. Adjusted operating margin climbed to 22.5%, surpassing guidance and more than doubling versus last year, while adjusted EPS hit a record $2.11, up 215%, signaling powerful operating leverage.
Optical networks, including interconnects, grew more than 45% year on year, with RLS and WAV server systems each advancing over 55%. The in-and-around-the-data-center segment has already quadrupled year to date, outpacing Ciena’s promised 3x growth as direct cloud provider revenue leapt more than 80%.
Q3 book-to-bill was well above 1, driving backlog up by $800 million to $8.5 billion. Management expects backlog to exceed $10 billion by the end of fiscal 2026, and noted that just one month into Q4, orders booked were already approaching the full level of Q3.
Executives described an extraordinary AI-led demand backdrop for bandwidth and connectivity, with total addressable market seen doubling from roughly $25 billion to about $50 billion by 2029. Ciena expects not only a larger market but also a rising share of that expanding pie.
WaveLogic 6 Extreme Extends Technology Lead
WaveLogic 6 Extreme remains the only 1.6 terabit high-performance modem commercially available, 18 months after launch. Its ramp has already surpassed the prior-generation WaveLogic 5e, with growing adoption across both traditional wide-area networks and emerging AI WAN architectures.
RLS Strength and Hyper-Rail Build Momentum
Ciena’s RLS intelligent line systems hold an estimated 70% share and are viewed as the industry standard for disaggregated line systems. Orders for next-gen RLS Hyper-Rail are ramping, with initial customer standardization targeted by end-2026 and material revenue expected as scale builds from 2027 onward.
WaveLogic 5 nano pluggable optics continued to ramp, with Q3 shipments of 800ZR modules more than doubling quarter on quarter. The company highlighted strong interest in Nitro for active copper cables and early sample orders for Vesta, its open co-packaged optical solution aimed at next-generation data center architectures.
Ciena announced a notable hyperscaler victory, integrating WaveLogic 6 coherent technology directly into the customer’s own platform. The design combines Ciena’s DSPs, drivers, TIAs, and optical expertise into a full module slated for broad rollout across the client’s global optical footprint.
Adjusted gross margin reached 46.4%, up 450 basis points year on year and near the top of guidance even excluding a one-time tariff refund benefit. Management said disciplined costs, mix and pricing let them reset the margin baseline firmly in the mid-40s, with further expansion expected over the coming years.
Solid Free Cash Flow and Ample Liquidity
Despite higher working capital needs to support inventory and revenue growth, Ciena generated $116 million in free cash flow in Q3. The company ended the quarter with $2.8 billion in cash and equivalents, providing significant flexibility to invest in capacity, technology, and shareholder returns.
A June convertible offering gave Ciena a five-year zero-coupon instrument with a 114% economic conversion premium, enabling repayment of a 5.5% term loan. The company also repurchased 356,000 shares for $172 million in Q3, signaling confidence in long-term prospects and valuation.
Capital investments boosted capacity enough to support more than 60% year-to-date growth in RLS plug and WAV server revenue. Ciena has locked in long-term component agreements through 2029, is qualifying additional suppliers, and is exploring new technologies to strengthen supply resilience.
Customer discussions now include price increases from high single digits into the high teens or low twenties depending on product, with some hikes applied to backlog. Negotiations also encompass payment terms, fill rates, and mutual supply commitments, reflecting a broader value exchange rather than pure price hikes.
Around half of Ciena’s business now comes directly from hyperscalers, with neo-scalers expected to grow more important in 2027 and 2028. Demand spans RLS, Hyper-Rail, modems, MOFN, submarine networks and data center connectivity, with activity reported in India, the Middle East, North America and Asia.
Service Provider and Submarine Growth Tailwinds
Management sees steady service provider growth ahead, driven by years of underinvestment and renewed optical buildouts, including MOFN projects. Massive global submarine cable deployments, where Ciena claims the number-one market share, add another long-lived growth vector.
Scale-Across and Existing Data Center Focus
Scale-across connectivity between data centers was described as a major, still early-stage demand driver, particularly for North American hyperscalers. Much of the current visibility ties to existing facilities, GPU refresh cycles, capacity additions, inference traffic and network expansion rather than just new builds.
Software and Embedded Intelligence Still Matter
Web-scale deals tend to include fewer off-box software components, but Ciena stressed that customers still receive advanced on-box intelligence. These include protection mechanisms, planning and link-engineering tools, plus global service capabilities that underpin activation and service-level performance.
Attractive Economics for Hyper-Rail and Coherent
Management expects Hyper-Rail margins to be a step function above the already improved RLS profile, becoming accretive as volumes rise through 2027-2029. Ciena also sees coherent optics inside data centers as a major emerging market, with its planned 3.2-terabit solution positioned to capture early leadership.
Executives noted that fiscal 2027 revenue could exceed current guidance if more supply were available, but capacity remains limiting. The company cannot meet all backlog delivery requests for 2027 and expects the supply-demand imbalance to persist into 2028.
Ciena anticipates lower cash from operations in Q4, as it deploys capital to secure long-term supply agreements and upstream capacity. While this reduces near-term cash conversion, management views the spending as essential to support multiyear growth and customer commitments.
Working-Capital Cash Conversion Volatility
Quarterly working-capital cash conversion slipped versus the prior quarter, reflecting inventory and supply investments. However, executives said the broader trend versus year-ago levels remains positive, suggesting improving structural cash dynamics over time.
Tariff Refunds One-Off; Canadian Risk Monitored
The roughly 70-basis-point Q3 gross-margin boost from tariff refunds was a one-time accounting item that will not recur. Ciena is also assessing a new Canadian tariff regime that could carry a roughly $10 million quarterly impact and is pursuing mitigation strategies.
The R-S DCOM business is a net new addition that management describes as accretive to profitability. Still, revenue from this segment is expected to be lumpy quarter to quarter because of customer concentration and project timing.
Lower Off-Box Software in Web-Scale Deals
Management again acknowledged that web-scale contracts tend to include fewer separate software products than traditional deals. The company believes embedded software, tools and services still deliver substantial value and help support pricing and long-term relationships.
Ciena now expects fiscal 2026 operating expenses of about $1.6 billion, up from the earlier $1.5 billion view, including one-time variable compensation. Management plans to reinvest those amounts and further fund line systems and interconnect innovation to sustain competitiveness.
Guidance Signals Sustained Growth and Margin Strength
For Q4 fiscal 2026, Ciena guides revenue to about $1.75 billion, plus or minus $50 million, with adjusted gross margins near 45% and operating margin around 20%. For fiscal 2027, management projects revenue growth of at least 30% to $8.3-$8.4 billion, gross margin of 45-46%, operating margin of 25-27%, and a ramp of Hyper-Rail to several hundred million dollars.
Ciena’s earnings call painted a picture of a company riding powerful AI and optical networking tailwinds while carefully managing capacity, pricing and investment. Record financial results, rising backlog and strong technology positioning underpin a bullish long-term view, even as supply bottlenecks, tariffs and near-term cash outlays introduce some tactical challenges for investors to monitor.

Angola Cables Boosts Capacity Across MONET and SACS Submarine Cable Systems with Ciena Technology
Ciena (CIEN)’s optical innovations power 800 Gb/s services across key transatlantic routes spanning 12,780 kilometers connecting the United States, Brazil, and Angola
Angola Cables, a multinational telecommunications and digital solutions provider, is leveraging Ciena’s (NYSE: CIEN) high-capacity optical technology to bolster its transatlantic network for hyperscale, cloud, and AI-driven traffic across the MONET and South Atlantic Cable System (SACS) submarine cable systems.
MONET spans 10,556 km between the United States and Brazil, while SACS bridges Brazil to Angola as the first South Atlantic crossing with 6,165 km. By combining these systems, data can travel directly between Angola and the United States in 130 milliseconds round trip delay (RTD). Ciena’s technology will enable Angola Cables to support surging bandwidth demands driven by data-intensive AI models and cloud services. The solutions will also help Angola Cables simplify network operations through innovative software control and management capabilities.
“Our submarine cable systems are a critical digital bridge connecting Africa with the Americas, offering a diverse and secure route between these continents, while demand from hyperscalers and cloud providers continues to accelerate,” said Adriano Caldevilla, CTO, Angola Cables. “Together with Ciena, we will enhance the scale, flexibility, and intelligence of our subsea infrastructure to help customers build and expand AI-ready networks while maximizing the performance of our existing fiber assets.”
Angola Cables will deploy Ciena's Waveserver powered by WaveLogic 6 Extreme (WL6e), 6500 Packet-Optical platform, and Navigator Network Control Suite to increase the capacity and performance of its existing subsea network while creating more flexible route options for hyperscale, cloud, wholesale, content, and enterprise customers. The deployment will help Angola Cables deliver high-capacity connectivity across key routes linking the United States, Brazil and Africa, including 800G client interfaces on MONET.
“Demand for AI, cloud services, and digital applications is accelerating the need for higher-capacity, more intelligent networks,” said Fernando Capella, Regional Director for CALA South, Ciena. “Ciena's coherent optical and software solutions lay the foundation for AI-ready connectivity across the Atlantic, enabling Angola Cables to support hyperscalers and cloud providers with scalable, high-performance connectivity.”
This network upgrade will give Angola Cables the ability to offer customers diverse, high-capacity and resilient routes. The deployment builds on Angola Cables’ previous use of Ciena technology across its subsea network. Ciena's solution further enhances the network’s flexibility and scalability allowing capacities ranging from a single 100 Gbps to a full fiber pair, catering to a wide range of connectivity needs, including spectrum and MOFN (Managed Optical Fiber Networks).

Ciena Corp.
Interested in Ciena Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.
Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani upgraded Ciena to Outperform with a $550 price target, citing optical networking as an overlooked AI infrastructure bottleneck.
Ciena's stock fell more than 40% from its June high but has climbed about 17% in less than three weeks amid renewed investor interest.
Ciena posted 37% year-over-year revenue growth and 215% EPS growth, with a backlog expected to exceed $10 billion by fiscal year-end.
Despite all the money pouring into the artificial intelligence boom, it feels like only a small handful of names have been consistent winners.
Plenty of companies quietly making that boom possible have been overlooked, their shares languishing while the giants soar. Ciena Corporation (NYSE: CIEN) is a good example.
Despite sitting right in the path of the AI wave, its stock has nonetheless tumbled more than 40% from its June high. However, that disconnect may be correcting itself.
After a punishing slide, the stock appears to have found a floor early this month and has started to turn higher, climbing around 17% in less than three weeks.
Even after its fall, Ciena is still up roughly 50% for the year, and the current bounce suggests investors are beginning to look again at a name they had written off. A well-timed vote of confidence from Wall Street this week has helped, making this a perfect time to ask if the market has been way too negative on Ciena’s prospects.
That vote of confidence came from Evercore ISI, with analyst Amit Daryanani upgrading Ciena to Outperform earlier this week and setting a $550 price target. From where the stock trades today, that's around 50% upside, and just as importantly, Daryanani's argument cuts to the heart of the bull case: that Ciena sits at one of the AI boom's most overlooked bottlenecks.
This bottleneck theory is simple. Amid all the noise about chips and computing power, far less attention goes to how that data actually moves around. Modern AI systems shuttle staggering volumes of information between and within data centers, and doing so fast enough has become a serious constraint on how powerful they can be. Daryanani pinpointed connectivity as an increasingly critical bottleneck to the pace of AI's advancement.
This is Ciena's world. The company specializes in optical networking, the high-speed connections that carry data over long distances and, increasingly, across the sprawling AI facilities springing up everywhere. As one of the few dedicated names in the field, it’s particularly well placed to benefit as those systems, and their data demands, keep growing.
The bullish case is more than a story, because the numbers behind it are seriously impressive. In its most recent quarterly report, released earlier this month, Ciena reported year-on-year revenue growth of 37% and earnings per share growth of 215%.
More telling still is the pipeline of future work. Ciena’s management pointed to a swelling order book, with its backlog expected to top $10 billion by the end of its financial year, giving it, and the market, solid visibility into future revenue.
Ciena is also pushing into new territory. Beyond its traditional strength in long-distance links, it's developing products that operate inside data centers themselves, chasing a market it believes could be worth many billions. With leading technology and a clutch of new products, it has several ways to win rather than relying on a single one.
None of this means the risks have vanished. The stock's steep fall from its June high and the volatility that followed remind us how quickly sentiment can turn on a name like this. The biggest worry is simply that the AI spending spree may not last, and Ciena's fortunes are tightly bound to how much the cloud giants keep investing, so any slowdown would hit its orders hard.
There’s also the matter of who its customers are. A handful of large clients account for a hefty slice of Ciena's revenue, with one customer alone making up close to 20%. Such concentration cuts both ways: it’s fine while those customers spend freely, but it would hurt if even one pulled back.
Weighing it up, Ciena makes a compelling case as an underappreciated way to play the AI infrastructure boom. It sits at a real bottleneck, its core business is growing fast, its order book offers rare visibility, and Wall Street is clearly leaning toward the upside.
The caution comes not from the bulls but from the setup itself. Ciena's shares remain volatile, its valuation demands strong growth for years to come, and expectations will likely stay high after this week's upgrade. That tension, between an early-stage turnaround and a business with a lot still to prove, is what keeps the stock finely balanced.
For those who believe the AI buildout has years left to run, though, Ciena increasingly looks like one of its more overlooked beneficiaries, and this week's upgrade is a clear sign that others are already catching on.

On September 3, 2026, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN) reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 results for the period ended August 1, 2026. Revenue rose 37% year-over-year to $1.67 billion, adjusted earnings per share more than tripled to $2.11, and backlog grew $800 million in the quarter to $8.5 billion. Adjusted gross margin reached 46.4% and adjusted operating margin hit a record 22.5%.
On September 16, 2026, Ciena held its Investor Forum in Ottawa and announced fiscal 2029 targets: roughly 30% revenue CAGR from 2026 through 2029, approximately 50% adjusted gross margin, adjusted operating margin of 32% to 35%, and free cash flow margin of approximately 20%.
Bulls: A Durable AI Buildout, Now Backed By a Concrete Multiyear Framework
Citi called the September 4 post-earnings selloff a buying opportunity, keeping a Buy rating and a $658 price target, arguing that management’s initial 30% growth guidance for fiscal 2027 is “a floor that will move higher with increased supply.”
JPMorgan kept an Overweight rating, saying Ciena Corporation “set a strong initial fiscal 2027 floor” as demand continues to build. The firm cut its price target on the stock from $635 to $605.
After the investor forum, Northland raised its target to $550 from $500, keeping Outperform, saying the 2029 targets point to earnings power of $25 or more per share with upside potential.
Rosenblatt reiterated Buy with a $525 target, calling the fiscal 2029 framework “promising” and noting the demand commentary reads through positively for Nokia as the other scaled optical data center interconnect vendor. Barclays raised its target to $548 from $475, staying Overweight.
The operating detail backs the optimism: bookings in the first month of the fourth quarter nearly matched all of the third quarter’s orders, management now projects more than $10 billion in backlog by year end with visibility into fiscal 2028, optical networking revenue rose 46% to $1.19 billion, and cloud provider revenue grew more than 80%.
Bears: Even After the Raise, Supply and Margin Questions Haven’t Gone Away
Morgan Stanley kept an Equal Weight rating both before and after the forum, cutting its target to $425 from $490 on September 4 over supply as a “key constraint,” then raising it only modestly to $450 on September 17, saying it wants “a couple more quarters” of new products flowing through before gross margin becomes the catalyst it needs to see.
TD Cowen cut its target sharply to $400 from $575 on September 4, despite keeping a Buy rating, calling the guide “seemingly disappointing to bulls” even with strong operating leverage.
B. Riley cut its target to $347 from $413, keeping Neutral, citing multiple compression across AI-related optical stocks broadly.
The costs of chasing demand are real: cash from operations is expected to decline in the fourth quarter as Ciena disperses funds to support long-term component agreements through 2029, two customers made up 41.7% of revenue, and roughly 70 basis points of the 46.4% adjusted gross margin came from a one-time tariff refund that will not repeat.
Arrowstreet Capital increased its position 21% to 1.68 million shares worth $822.7 million as of the second quarter of 2026, and AQR Capital Management added 8% to reach 1.05 million shares worth $507.2 million. Jericho Capital Asset Management cut its stake 67% to 561,513 shares worth $275.5 million.
Overall hedge fund ownership rose to 81 funds from 73 the prior quarter. Short interest sits at just 2.3% of float, a level consistent with the wave of target increases that followed the investor forum, and shares trade at 39.37 times forward earnings as of September 18, 2026.
The two rounds of commentary tell the story better than either one alone. On September 4, several firms cut targets despite the beat because they wanted proof that the demand Ciena Corporation described could translate into a real multiyear commitment rather than a supply-constrained expectation.
By September 17, after Ciena Corporation put concrete numbers behind that commitment, several firms raised targets again. What has not changed is the remaining question Morgan Stanley keeps asking: whether gross margin actually climbs toward that 50% target as Hyper-Rail and new interconnect products ramp, or whether supply constraints keep capping the pace for another year.

Coherent, Lumentum, and Ciena stocks surge on bullish Wall Street call
Grace O'Donnell · Editor, Special Projects
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 1:09 PM PDT 2 min read
Optical networking stocks ripped higher on Thursday after Wall Street grew bullish on the next generation of data center networking.
Coherent (COHR) stock jumped 11%, while Lumentum (LITE) increased 7%. Ciena (CIEN) gained 7%, and Arista (ANET) rose 0.4% after Bernstein called the group structural AI winners in a note initiating coverage with an Outperform rating.

Coherent led the pack on Thursday after launching an optics platform for AI infrastructure, dubbed PhotonLink.
PhotonLink packages Coherent's services, photonics technologies, and components, including lasers, fibers, and detectors, into one platform for AI data centers. The company said it already has 20 customer engagements, split between co-packaged optic (CPO) and near-packaged optic (NPO) assemblies, as well as five engagements "in emerging chip-to-chip connectivity."
"The next leap in AI requires more than faster chips — it requires a new way to connect them," Coherent CEO Jim Anderson said in a statement. "Customers need complete optical solutions, not just individual components."
An employee walks next to server racks at the PA10 data center operated by Equinix in Saint-Denis, near Paris, France, June 4, 2026. REUTERS/Benoit Tessier · REUTERS / REUTERS
As demand for AI compute grows, companies are looking to make data center connections faster and more energy-efficient than the copper wiring commonly used today.
In April, Goldman Sachs called optical networking "the next mega trend in AI infrastructure," roughly a month after Nvidia (NVDA) announced a $4 billion investment in Coherent and Lumentum.
"Along with an AI infrastructure ramp-up and rising computing power per rack, we expect all configurations to enjoy strong growth ahead, opening a further 9x TAM unlock to US$154bn," the Goldman Sachs team wrote.
Investors have bought up optics stocks in hopes that they're the next AI leaders. Today's gains add to an impressive rally for the group year to date. Coherent stock has risen 73%, Lumentum 183%, Ciena 62%, and Arista 56% in 2026.

Ciena (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock is up 5% to $351.38 in early Friday afternoon trading, extending a rebound that’s now stretched across the full week. The move reverses the post-earnings selloff that followed Ciena’s September 3 fiscal third quarter release. Today’s advance has effectively closed the door on the initial negative reaction to the report and pushed the stock back through the level it held before the release.
The bid extends well beyond Ciena today. Arista (NYSE:ANET) stock is up 5% to $197.84, and Cisco (NASDAQ:CSCO) stock is up 4% to $111.53. All three networking names are climbing by a multiple of the broader sector’s move, and each is doing so on the same session without individual company news to explain it.
The wider technology sector is trading much calmer than the networking group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.5%, and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 1%. Buyers are giving an extra boost to certain networking equipment stock rather than massively sweeping technology and large-cap indexes as a whole.
No company announcement, contract award, guidance revision or regulatory decision was published by Ciena this session to explain the same-day move. The pattern across Ciena, Arista and Cisco reads like money rotating into the transport and switching layer as a group rather than a single-name catalyst. Each of the three covers a distinct slice of that stack, and today’s session is treating them together in a way that hasn’t been true every week this quarter.
Ciena supplies the optical transport equipment that carries traffic between and inside data centers, Arista supplies the switching layer above it, and Cisco supplies networking equipment across both enterprise and service provider customers, the same infrastructure layer we mapped out in a free report on seven AI buildout suppliers that aren’t chipmakers. The gap between the group’s move and the sector fund’s move makes today look like a real rotation, since Ciena, Arista and Cisco are each running well ahead of IYW and SPY. That framing puts the day’s story on infrastructure demand rather than on any one company’s balance sheet.
What Separates Ciena From Arista and Cisco
What separates Ciena from Arista and Cisco right now is the week rather than the day. Ciena stock had the most ground to make up after its fiscal third quarter release, and Friday’s climb has taken the stock to a 10.7% gain since last Friday. Arista stock and Cisco stock are running nearly as hard today without a comparable setback behind them.
That difference shapes how the day reads for CIEN shareholders. The recovery has already carried Ciena stock past most of the ground it lost after the earnings release, and further upside from here would need buyers who haven’t chased the group yet or a fresh catalyst that draws in longer-duration capital. Ciena’s setup now reads as a decision point for anyone who sat out the initial bounce, since the easy part of the gap has already filled.
For Arista and Cisco, the story is simpler. Both stocks are climbing on the group bid without an earnings hangover to work through, so today’s move looks like fresh momentum rather than a recovery. The open question is whether the two can carry the group’s leadership if Ciena stock’s post-earnings gap finishes closing before Monday.
The key tell into Friday’s close is whether Ciena, Arista and Cisco shares all hold their gains into the bell. A firm close across the three would frame the narrow networking bid as a genuine rotation rather than an intraday burst. A softer finish for Arista or Cisco could pull Ciena stock’s rebound back before next week begins.
Traders can watch for whether the group’s leadership carries into next week’s action or fades once Ciena’s earnings gap fully closes. Your networking-stock exposure could stay measured until that leadership holds through a second session at the same intensity, since two consecutive sessions of outsized moves would carry a different weight than a single afternoon.
For now, Ciena stock remains the swing name in this group. The stock has both the freshest scar and the strongest week behind it, so its behavior over the next few sessions may set the tone for how the rotation is priced across Arista and Cisco. Arista stock and Cisco stock can follow the leadership, and their charts look cleaner, though CIEN is the one carrying the recovery story into next week and the one in which the risk-and-reward gap looks widest.
